sentences.zh: 申徽 陸通 厙狄峙 楊荐 王慶 趙剛 趙昶 王悅 趙文表 元定 楊摽

translations.literal: Shen Hui, Lu Tong, She Dishi, Yang Jian, Wang Qing, Zhao Gang, Zhao Chang, Wang Yue, Zhao Wenbiao, Yuan Ding, Yang Biao
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui, Lu Tong, She Dishi, Yang Jian, Wang Qing, Zhao Gang, Zhao Chang, Wang Yue, Zhao Wenbiao, Yuan Ding, and Yang Biao

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十七

translations.literal: Biographies 57
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 57

sentences.zh: 申徽陸通弟逞厙狄峙楊薦王慶趙剛子仲卿趙昶王悅趙文表元定楊

translations.literal: Shen Hui; Lu Tong and his younger brother Cheng; She Dishi; Yang Jian; Wang Qing; Zhao Gang and his son Zhongqing; Zhao Chang; Wang Yue; Zhao Wenbiao; Yuan Ding; Yang—
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui; Lu Tong and his younger brother Cheng; She Dishi; Yang Jian; Wang Qing; Zhao Gang and his son Zhongqing; Zhao Chang; Wang Yue; Zhao Wenbiao; Yuan Ding; Yang—

sentences.zh: 申徽，字世儀，魏郡人也。

translations.literal: Shen Hui, courtesy name Shiyi, was a native of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui, whose courtesy name was Shiyi, came from Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖鐘，為後趙司徒。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zhong served as Minister over the Masses under Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his ancestor Zhong had been minister over the masses under Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 冉閔末，中原喪亂，鐘子邃避地江左。

translations.literal: At the end of the reign of Ran Min, the Central Plains fell into chaos, and Zhong's son Sui fled south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Min's rule collapsed and the heartland was torn by war, Zhong's son Sui took refuge south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖爽，仕宋，位雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shuang served the Song and held the post of Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shuang had served the Liu Song as governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 祖隆道。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Longdao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Longdao.

sentences.zh: 宋北兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He had been Northern Governor of Yan Province under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: He had held the northern Yanzhou post under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父明仁，郡功曹，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Mingren was a commandery merit officer and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingren had been a commandery merit officer and died young.

sentences.zh: 徽少與母居，盡力孝養。

translations.literal: When Hui was young he lived with his mother and devoted himself fully to filial care.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he lived with his mother and gave himself wholly to caring for her.

sentences.zh: 及長，好經史。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he took to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 性審慎，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious and did not make friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious by nature and did not court casual friendships.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，喪畢，乃歸於魏。

translations.literal: After his mother's death, when the mourning period was over, he returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and the mourning was finished, he went back north to Wei.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以元邃為東徐州刺史，邃引徽為主簿。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yuan Sui was made Governor of Eastern Xu Province, and Sui brought Hui in as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Yuan Sui was made governor of eastern Xu, and Sui took Hui on as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，邃被檻車送洛陽，故吏賓客並委去，唯徽送之。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Sui was sent to Luoyang in a prisoner cart; former subordinates and guests all abandoned him, and only Hui escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao's defeat Sui was carted off to Luoyang in bonds; every former retainer and guest deserted him—only Hui went along.

sentences.zh: 及邃得免，乃廣集賓友，歎徽有古人風。

translations.literal: When Sui was released, he gathered many guests and friends and praised Hui for having the bearing of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sui was freed, he called his friends together and marveled that Hui had the steadfastness of men of old.

sentences.zh: 尋除太尉府行參軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed acting staff officer in the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made an acting staff officer in the grand commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，徽以洛陽兵難未已，遂間行入關見周文。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, because warfare around Luoyang had not ceased, Hui made his way by hidden routes into the passes to see Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, with fighting still raging around Luoyang, Hui stole through byways into the passes to seek out Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周文與語，奇之，薦之于賀拔岳，嶽亦雅相敬待，引為賓客。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou spoke with him, found him remarkable, and recommended him to Heba Yue; Yue too treated him with refined respect and took him on as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen talked with him, was struck by his gifts, and commended him to Heba Yue, who likewise received him with honor and kept him as a client.

sentences.zh: 周文臨夏州，以徽為記室參軍，兼府主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took up post at Xia Province, he made Hui recorder in the secretariat and concurrently chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen went to Xia province, he made Hui his recording secretary and chief clerk of the staff.

sentences.zh: 周文察徽沉密有度量，每事信委之，乃為大行台郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw that Hui was deep, careful, and measured; he entrusted him with every matter and made him a gentleman-attendant of the Grand Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Hui was steady, discreet, and far-sighted, Emperor Wen trusted him with one affair after another and appointed him gentleman-attendant of the grand commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，幕府務殷，四方書檄皆徽之辭也。

translations.literal: At that time the army and state were newly founded, the headquarters was overwhelmed with business, and all letters and proclamations to the four directions were in Hui's phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: The state and army were still being built from nothing; the staff was swamped with work, and every dispatch to the four quarters bore Hui's pen.

sentences.zh: 以迎孝武功，封博平縣子、本州大中正。

translations.literal: For merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Boxing county and made chief rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu he was made viscount of Boxing and chief rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong his fief was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中書舍人，修起居注。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat and charged with compiling the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became attendant drafter at the secretariat and was put in charge of the court diary.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，大軍不利，近侍之官分散者眾，徽獨不離左右，魏帝稱歎之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao the main army met defeat; many of the close attendants scattered, but Hui alone did not leave the sovereign's side, and the Wei emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao the main force was beaten; most of the inner court fled, but Hui never left the emperor's side, and the Wei sovereign spoke of it with admiration.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was moved to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，東陽王元榮為瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Yuan Rong of Dongyang had been Governor of Gua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Yuan Rong of Dongyang had held Gua province.

sentences.zh: 其女婿劉彥隨焉。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Liu Yan accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Liu Yan went with him.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，瓜州首望表榮子康為刺史，彥遂殺康而取其位。

translations.literal: When Rong died, the leading families of Gua Province petitioned that Rong's son Kang be made governor; Yan then killed Kang and seized his post.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death the leading clans of Gua petitioned for Rong's son Kang as governor; Yan murdered Kang and took the post for himself.

sentences.zh: 屬四方多難，朝廷不遑問罪，因授彥刺史。

translations.literal: Trouble was rife in every quarter, and the court had no leisure to punish him, so Yan was confirmed as governor.
translations.idiomatic: With turmoil everywhere, the court could not spare the force to punish him and simply recognized Yan as governor.

sentences.zh: 頻徵不奉詔，又南通吐谷渾，將圖叛逆。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly summoned but would not obey the edicts; he also opened relations southward with Tuyuhun and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated summons went unanswered; he courted Tuyuhun to the south and was plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 周文難於動眾，欲以權略致之，乃以徽為河西大使，密令圖彥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou found it hard to move the army and wished to take him by stratagem; he therefore made Hui envoy to Hexi and secretly ordered him to deal with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was reluctant to march a host against him and meant to use craft instead; he made Hui envoy to Hexi with secret orders to bring Yan in.

sentences.zh: 徽輕以五十騎行，既至，止於賓館。

translations.literal: Hui traveled light with fifty horsemen; when he arrived, he lodged at the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Hui went with only fifty riders; on arrival he put up at the official guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 彥見徽單使，不以為疑，徽乃遣一人微勸彥歸朝，以揣其意，彥不從。

translations.literal: Yan saw that Hui was a lone envoy and was not suspicious; Hui then sent one man to urge Yan subtly to return to court and thereby probe his intent, but Yan would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, seeing a lone envoy, suspected nothing; Hui sent a man to sound him out on returning to court, but Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 徽又使贊成其住計，彥便從之，遂來至館。

translations.literal: Hui then had others support the plan that Yan should stay, and Yan went along with it and came to the guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's men then seconded a scheme for Yan to remain where he was; Yan agreed and came to the guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 徽先與瓜州豪右密謀執彥，遂叱而縛之。

translations.literal: Hui had already plotted secretly with the powerful families of Gua Province to seize Yan; he then shouted and had him bound.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had already conspired with Gua's great families; he shouted an order and had Yan bound on the spot.

sentences.zh: 彥辭無罪，徽數之曰：「君無尺寸之功，濫居方嶽之重，恃遠背誕，不恭貢職，戮辱使人，輕忽詔命。

translations.literal: Yan pleaded that he was guiltless; Hui recounted his crimes, saying: "You have not a finger's breadth of merit yet hold the weight of a frontier governor; relying on distance you turn your back on duty, neglect tribute, abuse envoys, and treat imperial orders lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan protested his innocence. Hui listed his offenses: "You have done nothing to earn your post yet hold a frontier governorship; you rely on distance to defy the court, neglect tribute, mistreat envoys, and treat the throne's orders with contempt.

sentences.zh: 計君之咎，實不容誅。

translations.literal: Weighing your offenses, they truly leave no room for pardon.
translations.idiomatic: By any reckoning your crimes admit no mercy.

sentences.zh: 但受詔之日，本令相送歸闕，所恨不得即申明罰，以謝邊遠耳。」

translations.literal: Yet on the day I received my orders I was charged only to escort you back to the capital; my one regret is that I cannot execute punishment on the spot to reassure the distant frontier."
translations.idiomatic: But the day I took my commission I was told only to bring you back to court; my sole regret is that I cannot punish you here and now to satisfy the borderlands."

sentences.zh: 於是宣詔慰勞吏人及彥所部，復雲大軍續至，城內無敢動者。

translations.literal: He then proclaimed the edict, comforted the officials and Yan's troops, and also announced that a great army was following; within the city none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He then read the edict, reassured the officials and Yan's men, and announced that a main force was on its way; no one in the city dared move.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was transferred to Minister of the Capital Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made minister of the capital offices.

sentences.zh: 十二年，瓜州刺史成慶為城人張保所殺，都督令狐延等起義逐保，啟請刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Governor Cheng Qing of Gua Province was killed by Zhang Bao, a man of the city; the commander-in-chief Linghu Yan and others rose in arms to drive Bao out and petitioned for a governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Governor Cheng Qing was killed by a townsman named Zhang Bao; Commander Linghu Yan and others rose against Bao and asked the court for a new governor.

sentences.zh: 以徽信洽西土，拜假節、瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Hui was trusted and well regarded in the western lands, he was appointed with provisional credentials as Governor of Gua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hui was trusted on the western frontier, he was given provisional authority as governor of Gua.

sentences.zh: 徽在州五稔，儉約率下，邊人樂而安之。

translations.literal: Hui was in the province for five years, frugal and restrained toward his subordinates; the border people were glad and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he governed the province, living plainly and leading by restraint; the frontier people were content and secure.

sentences.zh: 十六年，徽兼尚書右僕射，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Hui was made concurrently Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State Affairs, with additional titles of Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made vice director of the right while also holding palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, and grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，進爵為公，正右僕射，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed emperor his rank was advanced to duke, he was made full Vice Director of the Right, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei his fief rose to duke, he became full vice director of the right, and was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 徽性勤至，凡所居官，案牘無大小皆親自省覽，以是事無稽滯，吏不得為奸。

translations.literal: Hui was diligent to the utmost; in every office he held, documents great and small he personally examined, so that business did not pile up and clerks could not practice fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He was tirelessly thorough: in every post he read every document himself, great or small, so nothing stalled and his clerks could not cheat.

sentences.zh: 後雖曆公卿，此志不懈。

translations.literal: Later, though he rose through the ranks of chief ministers, he did not slacken in this resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose to the highest offices, he never let up.

sentences.zh: 出為襄州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 時南方初附，舊俗官人皆通餉遺。

translations.literal: The south had only lately submitted, and by old custom officials all exchanged gifts and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The south had only just been brought in, and by long custom officials exchanged gifts and favors freely.

sentences.zh: 徽性廉慎，乃畫楊震像於寢室以自戒。

translations.literal: Hui was by nature incorrupt and careful; he painted a portrait of Yang Zhen in his bedchamber to warn himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was scrupulously honest; he hung a portrait of Yang Zhen in his bedroom as a daily reminder.

sentences.zh: 及代還，人吏送者數十里不絕。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, officials and commoners who came to see him off stretched for several tens of li without a break.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, people and officials escorted him for miles without end.

sentences.zh: 徽自以無德於人，慨然懷愧，因賦詩，題于清水亭。

translations.literal: Hui felt he had done no real good for the people and was moved to shame; he therefore composed a poem and inscribed it at Qingshui Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he had earned no real gratitude, he was ashamed and wrote a poem, which he posted at Qingshui Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 長幼聞之，皆競來就讀，遞相謂曰：「此是申使君手跡。」

translations.literal: Young and old heard of it and all rushed to read it, saying to one another: "This is Envoy Shen's own hand."
translations.idiomatic: Young and old alike came to read it, telling one another, "This is Governor Shen's own writing."

sentences.zh: 並寫誦之。

translations.literal: They all copied it out and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: They copied it down and memorized it.

sentences.zh: 明帝以禦正任總絲綸，更崇其秩為上大夫，員四人，號大禦正，又以徽為之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because the office of Imperial Rectifier oversaw all drafting, raised its rank to Senior Grand Master with four incumbents, titled Grand Imperial Rectifier, and again appointed Hui to it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, holding that the imperial rectifier controlled all drafting, raised the post to senior grand master with four holders styled grand imperial rectifier, and again appointed Hui.

sentences.zh: 曆小司空、少保，出為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Junior Minister of Works and Junior Guardian, then went out as Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of junior minister of works and junior guardian, then went out as governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 入為小司徒、小宗伯。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Minister of Education and Junior Director of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as junior minister of education and junior director of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，上疏乞骸骨，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he submitted a memorial asking to retire; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he asked to retire; the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈泗州刺史，諡曰章。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Governor of Si Province, with the posthumous title Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Si, with the posthumous name Zhang.

sentences.zh: 子康嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位瀘州刺史、司織下大夫、上開府。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Governor of Lu Province, Junior Grand Master of the Weaving Office, and Senior Opener of the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Lu, junior grand master of the weaving office, and senior opener of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 康弟敦，汝南郡守。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Dun was Administrator of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Dun was administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 敦弟靜，齊郡守。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Jing was administrator of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 靜弟處，上開府、同昌縣侯。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Chu was Senior Opener of the Headquarters and Marquis of Tongchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Chu was senior opener of the headquarters and marquis of Tongchang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 陸通，字仲明，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Tong, courtesy name Zhongming, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, whose courtesy name was Zhongming, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖載，從宋武帝平關中，軍還，留載隨其子義真鎮長安，遂沒赫連氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zai followed Emperor Wu of Song in pacifying Guanzhong; when the army returned, Zai was left with the emperor's son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an and was then lost to the Helian clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zai had followed Emperor Wu of Song in pacifying Guanzhong; when the army withdrew, Zai was left with the emperor's son Yizhen to hold Chang'an and fell into Helian hands.

sentences.zh: 魏太武平赫連氏，載仕魏，位中山郡守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei pacified the Helian, Zai entered Wei service and became Administrator of Zhongshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu of Wei destroyed the Helian, Zai served Wei as administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 父政，性致孝。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was by nature profoundly filial.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was deeply filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 其母吳人，好食魚。

translations.literal: His mother was a woman of Wu and loved to eat fish.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was from Wu and loved fish.

sentences.zh: 北土魚少，政求之常苦難。

translations.literal: Fish were scarce in the northern lands, and Zheng often found it hard to obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Fish were scarce in the north, and Zheng often struggled to find them.

sentences.zh: 後宅側忽有泉出，而有魚，遂得以供膳。

translations.literal: Later a spring suddenly appeared beside the house with fish in it, and he was thus able to supply her meals.
translations.idiomatic: Then a spring suddenly welled up beside the house with fish in it, so he could feed her at last.

sentences.zh: 時人以為孝感所致，因謂其泉為孝魚泉。

translations.literal: People of the time took it as the effect of filial feeling and therefore called the spring the Filial-Fish Spring.
translations.idiomatic: People said it was filial devotion answering him, and called the spring the Filial-Fish Spring.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃天光討伐。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Tianguang on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 及天光敗，歸周文。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated, he went over to Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang fell, he joined Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周文為行台，以政為行台左丞、原州長史，賜爵中都縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was Commissioner-in-Chief, he made Zheng Left Assistant of the Commissionerate and Chief Clerk of Yuan Province, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Zhongdu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen headed the commissionerate, he made Zheng left assistant commissioner and chief clerk of Yuan province, and enfeoffed him as baron of Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 大統中，卒。

translations.literal: During Datong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Datong era.

sentences.zh: 通少敦敏好學，有志節。

translations.literal: Tong in youth was earnest, quick, and fond of learning, with firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Tong was earnest, quick-witted, and studious, with a strong sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 幼從政在河西，遂逢寇難，與政相失。

translations.literal: As a child he followed Zheng to Hexi and there met with bandit troubles and was separated from his father.
translations.idiomatic: Still a boy, he followed his father to Hexi; bandits struck, and he was separated from Zheng.

sentences.zh: 通乃自拔東歸，從爾硃榮。

translations.literal: Tong then made his way east on his own and followed Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Tong made his own way east and entered the service of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮死，又從爾硃兆。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death he served Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃氏滅，及入關。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan was destroyed, he entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu were destroyed, he went into the passes.

sentences.zh: 周文時在夏州，引為帳內督。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou was then at Xia Province and took him on as commander within the tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was then at Xia province and made him a commander of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 頃之，賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害。

translations.literal: Before long Heba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Heba Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 時有傳嶽軍府已亡散者，周文憂之，通以為不然。

translations.literal: At the time there were reports that Yue's headquarters had already disbanded; Emperor Wen was troubled, but Tong did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Yue's army had scattered; Emperor Wen was alarmed, but Tong did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 居數日，問至，果如所策。

translations.literal: After several days inquiries arrived, and it was indeed as he had judged.
translations.idiomatic: Within days word came in, exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 自是愈見親禮，遂晝夜陪侍，家人罕見其面。

translations.literal: From then on he was ever more favored and attended day and night; his family rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was treated with ever greater intimacy, attending day and night; his family scarcely saw him.

sentences.zh: 通雖處機密，愈自恭謹，周文以此重之。

translations.literal: Though Tong was in confidential posts, he became only more respectful and careful, and Emperor Wen valued him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Though he stood at the center of secrets, he grew only more deferential, and Emperor Wen prized him for it.

sentences.zh: 後以迎孝武功，封都昌縣伯。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Duchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for helping welcome Emperor Xiaowu, he was made baron of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong his fief was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai and recovering Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai and recovering Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之後。

translations.literal: After Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 力戰有功。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 又從解洛陽圍。

translations.literal: He also followed in raising the siege of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped lift the siege of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍還，屬趙青雀反于長安，周文將討之，以人馬疲弊，不可速行，又謂青雀等一時陸梁，不足為慮，乃云「我到長安，但輕騎臨之，必當面縛。」

translations.literal: When the army returned, Zhao Qingque rebelled at Chang'an; Emperor Wen of Zhou was about to campaign against him, but men and horses were worn out and could not march quickly; he also thought Qingque and the rest were momentary upstarts and not worth concern, and said: "When I reach Chang'an I need only go with light cavalry and they will surely be bound before my face."
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Zhao Qingque rose in Chang'an; Emperor Wen meant to crush him, but men and horses were exhausted and could not move fast; he also thought Qingque's band were mere rabble and said, "When I reach Chang'an a light detachment will be enough—they will be bound before me at once."

sentences.zh: 通進曰：「青雀等既以大軍不利，謂朝廷傾危，同惡相求，遂成反亂。

translations.literal: Tong stepped forward and said: "Qingque and the rest, seeing that the main army had met defeat, believed the court was tottering; like evils they sought one another and thus formed a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Tong stepped forward: "Qingque and his fellows, seeing our main force defeated, think the dynasty is failing; villains have rallied to one another and made a real revolt.

sentences.zh: 然其逆謀久定，必無遷善之心。

translations.literal: Yet their treasonous design has long been fixed; they will certainly have no mind to turn to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Their plot has been set for some time; they will not turn back now.

sentences.zh: 且其詐言大軍敗績，東寇將至，若以輕騎往，百姓謂為信然，更沮兆庶之望。

translations.literal: Moreover they falsely claim the main army was defeated and eastern invaders are coming; if you go with light cavalry, the people will take it as true and the hopes of the masses will be further crushed.
translations.idiomatic: They also spread lies that our army was routed and eastern enemies are coming; if you ride in lightly, the people will believe it and lose heart entirely.

sentences.zh: 大兵雖疲弊，精銳猶多，以明公之威，率思歸之眾，以順討逆，何慮不平？」

translations.literal: Though the great army is weary, there are still many elite troops; with your lordship's authority, leading men who long to return home, to punish rebellion with righteousness—why worry that it will not be pacified?"
translations.idiomatic: Our host may be tired, but the picked troops are still numerous; with your prestige, leading men eager to go home, you can strike the rebels with justice—why doubt victory?"

sentences.zh: 周文深納之，因從平青雀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou deeply accepted this and then followed in pacifying Qingque.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen took this to heart and then joined the campaign that crushed Qingque.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，進爵為公，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Recording his services before and after, his rank was advanced to duke and he was made Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier and later merits were recognized: he was raised to duke and made governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 以寇難未平，留不之部。

translations.literal: Because bandit troubles were not yet settled, he was kept from going to his province.
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion still unsettled, he was kept from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 與于謹討劉平伏，加大都督。

translations.literal: With Yu Jin he campaigned against Liu Pingfu and was made Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Jin he campaigned against Liu Pingfu and was made grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從周文援玉壁，進儀同三司。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in relieving Yubi and was advanced to the honors of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wen to relieve Yubi and was raised to the honors of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 九年，高仲密以地來附，通從若干惠戰於芒山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Gao Zhongmi came over with his territory; Tong followed Ganluo Hui in battle at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Gao Zhongmi defected with his lands; Tong fought under Ganluo Hui at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 眾軍皆退，唯惠與通率所部力戰。

translations.literal: All the armies withdrew; only Hui and Tong led their units and fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Every other unit fell back; only Hui and Tong held their men and fought on.

sentences.zh: 至夜中乃陰引還，敵亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: At midnight they quietly withdrew, and the enemy did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they slipped away under cover, and the enemy did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 時授驃騎大將軍、開府僕同三司、太僕卿，賜姓部六孤氏，進爵綏德郡公。

translations.literal: At the time he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes, and Minister of the Stud; he was granted the surname Bulugu and advanced to Duke of Suide commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made general of agile cavalry, grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes, and minister of the stud; he received the surname Bulugu and was raised to duke of Suide.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐祚，拜小司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Tong was appointed Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended, Tong was made junior minister of works.

sentences.zh: 保定五年，累遷大司寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Baoding he was transferred in succession to Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Baoding he rose to grand minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 通性柔謹，雖久處列位，常清慎自守。

translations.literal: Tong was gentle and careful by nature; though he long held high rank, he always kept himself pure and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was mild and scrupulous; though he sat in high office for years, he always guarded his integrity.

sentences.zh: 所得祿賜，盡與親故共之，家無餘財。

translations.literal: All salary and gifts he received he shared entirely with kin and friends; his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away every stipend and gift to kin and friends, and left nothing at home.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「凡人患貧而不貴，不患貴而貧也。

translations.literal: He often said: "Most people fear being poor without being honored, not fearing being honored yet poor.
translations.idiomatic: He used to say, "People worry about being poor without rank, not about being ranked yet poor.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，轉大司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande he was transferred to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande he was made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 通弟逞。

translations.literal: Tong's younger brother was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's younger brother was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 逞字季明，初名彥，字世雄。

translations.literal: Cheng, courtesy name Jiming, was originally named Yan with the courtesy name Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, courtesy name Jiming, had originally been named Yan, with the courtesy name Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝常從容謂之曰：「爾既溫裕，何因乃字世雄？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once said to him at ease: "You are gentle and ample—why then is your courtesy name Shixiong?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once said to him gently, "You are mild and generous—why call yourself 'hero of the age'?

sentences.zh: 且為世之雄，非所宜也。

translations.literal: Moreover, to be a hero of the age is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, 'hero of the age' is hardly suitable.

sentences.zh: 于爾兄弟又復不類。」

translations.literal: Among your brothers it again does not match."
translations.idiomatic: It does not suit your brothers either."

sentences.zh: 遂改焉。

translations.literal: He then changed it.
translations.idiomatic: The name was changed.

sentences.zh: 逞少謹密，早有名譽。

translations.literal: Cheng in youth was careful and discreet and early gained a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Cheng was careful and discreet and won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 兄通先以軍功別受茅土，乃讓父爵中都縣伯令逞襲之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tong had first received a separate fief for military merit and therefore yielded their father's barony of Zhongdu county so that Cheng might inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tong had earned a separate fief for military merit and yielded their father's barony of Zhongdu so Cheng could inherit it.

sentences.zh: 起家羽林監、周文內親信。

translations.literal: He began his career as Supervisor of the Forest of Plumes and as a trusted intimate of Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as supervisor of the imperial guard and as a trusted intimate of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 時輩皆以驍勇自達，唯逞獨兼文雅，周文由此加禮遇焉。

translations.literal: His contemporaries all made their way through fierce courage; only Cheng combined literary refinement, and Emperor Wen for this reason treated him with added courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His peers all rose by martial prowess; Cheng alone combined learning and grace, and Emperor Wen honored him the more for it.

sentences.zh: 大統十四年，參大丞相府軍事，尋兼記室。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong he served on military affairs in the Grand Chancellor's headquarters and soon also held the post of recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Datong he joined the grand chancellor's military staff and soon doubled as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 保定初，累遷吏部中大夫，曆蕃部、禦伯中大夫，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，徙授司宗中大夫，轉軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he rose in succession to Senior Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel, served as Senior Grand Master in the Barbarian Affairs and Imperial Guard bureaus, was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes, was transferred to Senior Grand Master in the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, and then made Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoding he rose through the personnel ministry, held posts in the barbarian affairs and imperial guard bureaus, became general of agile cavalry and grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes, moved to the imperial clan directorate, and then became army marshal.

sentences.zh: 逞幹識詳明，歷任三府，所在著績。

translations.literal: Cheng was capable, perceptive, and thorough; he served in three headquarters and everywhere left a record of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was capable and clear-sighted; in three headquarters he left a mark wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 朝遷嘉之，進爵為公。

translations.literal: The court praised him and advanced his rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and raised his fief to duke.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，齊遣侍中斛斯文略、中書侍郎劉逖來聘。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe Qi sent Palace Attendant Husiwen Lue and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi sent palace attendant Husiwen Lue and secretariat gentleman Liu Ti on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 初修鄰好，盛選行人，詔逞為使主，尹公正為副以報之。

translations.literal: As good relations with a neighbor were newly established, envoys were chosen with great care; an edict named Cheng chief envoy and Yin Gongzheng deputy to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: With a new peace between neighbors, envoys were chosen with care; Cheng was named chief envoy and Yin Gongzheng his deputy for the return mission.

sentences.zh: 逞美容止，善辭令，敏而有禮，齊人稱焉。

translations.literal: Cheng had a fine appearance and bearing, was skilled in discourse, quick and courteous, and the people of Qi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was handsome, eloquent, quick-witted, and courteous; the Qi court praised him.

sentences.zh: 還屆近畿，詔令路車儀服郊迎而入，時人榮之。

translations.literal: On his return, when he reached the near capital districts, an edict ordered him welcomed into the city with state carriage, regalia, and suburban ceremony; men of the time took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital outskirts on his return, the court sent a state carriage and full ceremony to meet him at the suburbs; contemporaries counted it a great honor.

sentences.zh: 四年，除京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 郡界有豕生數子，經旬而死。

translations.literal: Within the commandery a sow farrowed several piglets that died after some ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery a sow farrowed several piglets that died within ten days.

sentences.zh: 其家又有豶，遂乳養之，諸豚賴之以活，時論以逞仁政所致。

translations.literal: That household also had a boar, which then nursed them; the piglets lived by this, and opinion of the time attributed it to Cheng's benevolent rule.
translations.idiomatic: The same household had a boar that nursed them instead; the piglets lived, and people said it was Cheng's humane government at work.

sentences.zh: 俄遷司會中大夫，出為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Senior Grand Master in the Directorate of Accounts and went out as Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made senior grand master of accounts and sent out as governor of He province.

sentences.zh: 晉公護雅重其才，表為中外府司馬，頗委任之。

translations.literal: Duke Jin Hu greatly valued his talent, recommended him as Army Marshal of the Inner and Outer Headquarters, and entrusted him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jin Hu prized his talent, had him made army marshal of the inner and outer headquarters, and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 尋復為司會，兼納言，遷小司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Director of Accounts, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and transferred to Junior Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again director of accounts, also censor-in-chief, then junior army marshal.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，坐免官。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Cheng was implicated and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was put to death, Cheng was dismissed as an associate.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起為納言。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又以疾不堪劇任，乃除宜州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of illness he could not bear heavy duties, and he was therefore appointed Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from heavy duties, so he was made governor of Yi province instead.

sentences.zh: 故事，刺史奉辭，例備鹵簿，逞以時屬農要，奏請停之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a governor took leave of the court he was furnished with a full guard of honor; Cheng, because the season was critical for farming, memorialized asking that this be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a departing governor was given a full guard of honor; Cheng, since it was planting season, asked that the ceremony be waived.

sentences.zh: 武帝深嘉焉，詔遂其所請，以彰雅操。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply commended this; an edict granted his request to display his refined conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised this warmly and granted his request to honor his restraint.

sentences.zh: 逞在州有惠政，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: Cheng in the province had benevolent administration, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he governed with kindness, and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 東宮初建，授太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was first established, he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's household was first set up, he was made grand tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand general.

sentences.zh: 子操嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 厙狄峙，其先遼東人，本姓段，匹磾之後也，因避難改焉。

translations.literal: She Dishi: his ancestors were from Liaodong; their original surname was Duan, and they were descendants of Pidi; because of taking refuge from troubles they changed it.
translations.idiomatic: She Dishi came of Liaodong stock; the clan had originally been named Duan and descended from Pidi, but changed the name while fleeing turmoil.

sentences.zh: 後徙居代，世為豪右。

translations.literal: Later they moved to Dai and for generations were powerful local families.
translations.idiomatic: They later settled in Dai and for generations were leading local magnates.

sentences.zh: 祖淩，武威郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ling was Administrator of Wuwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ling was administrator of Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父貞，上洛郡守。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Administrator of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen was administrator of Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 峙少以弘厚知名，善騎射，有謀略。

translations.literal: Dishi in youth was known for magnanimity and depth, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and had strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Dishi was known for generosity and steadiness, excelled at riding and archery, and had a strategist's mind.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，位高陽郡守，政存仁恕，百姓頗悅之。

translations.literal: He served Wei as Administrator of Gaoyang commandery; his government was humane and forgiving, and the people were quite pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he was administrator of Gaoyang; he governed with kindness and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，峙乃棄官從入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Dishi abandoned his office and followed him into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu went west, Dishi left his post and followed him into the passes.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，拜中書舍人，參掌機密，以恭謹見稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was appointed Attendant Drafting at the Secretariat, took part in confidential affairs, and was praised for respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he became attendant drafter at the secretariat, handled confidential matters, and was praised for his deference.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 時與東魏爭衡，蠕蠕乘虛，屢為邊患，朝議欲結和親，乃使峙往。

translations.literal: At the time they were contending with Eastern Wei; the Rouran seized the opportunity and repeatedly became a frontier menace; court discussion favored a marriage alliance, and Dishi was sent.
translations.idiomatic: While the court fought Eastern Wei, the Rouran raided the frontier again and again; the court decided on a marriage alliance and sent Dishi.

sentences.zh: 峙狀貌魁梧，善於辭令，蠕蠕主雅信重之，自是不復為寇。

translations.literal: Dishi was tall and imposing in appearance and skilled in discourse; the Rouran ruler greatly trusted and honored him, and from then on they no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: Dishi was tall and imposing and spoke well; the Rouran khan trusted him, and from then on they ceased raiding.

sentences.zh: 周文謂峙曰：「昔魏絳和戎，見稱前史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou said to Dishi: "In former times Wei Jiang made peace with the Rong and was praised in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Dishi, "Long ago Wei Jiang made peace with the Rong and won praise in the histories.

sentences.zh: 以君方之，彼有愧色。」

translations.literal: Compared with you, he would look ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Set beside you, he would blush."

sentences.zh: 封高邑縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made duke of Gaoyi county.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，拜侍中。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes and was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of agile cavalry and grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes and became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕滅後，突厥強盛，雖與周通好，而外連齊氏。

translations.literal: After the Rouran were destroyed the Turks grew powerful; though they were on good terms with Zhou, outwardly they also allied with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Rouran fell the Turks grew strong; though friendly with Zhou, they also courted Qi.

sentences.zh: 周文又令峙銜命喻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou again ordered Dishi to bear credentials and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen again sent Dishi with credentials to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 突厥感悟，即執齊使歸諸京師。

translations.literal: The Turks were moved to understanding and at once seized the Qi envoys and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks took his point, seized the Qi envoys, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 進爵安豐郡公，曆小司空、小司寇。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Anfeng commandery; he served as Junior Minister of Works and Junior Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke of Anfeng and served as junior minister of works and junior minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，為益州刺史、都督三十一州諸軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was made Governor of Yi Province and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for thirty-one provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign he was governor of Yi and commander-in-chief over thirty-one provinces.

sentences.zh: 峙性寬和，尚清靖，為夷獠所安。

translations.literal: Dishi was by nature broad and gentle, valued clarity and quiet, and was a source of peace for the Yi and Liao peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Dishi was easygoing and valued calm rule; the tribal peoples of the southwest were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 後為宜州刺史，入為少師。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Yi Province, then entered the capital as Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he governed Yi province, then returned to court as junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 以年老，乞骸骨，詔許之。

translations.literal: Because of old age he asked to retire; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he asked to retire, and the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子嶷嗣，少知名，位開府儀同三司、職方中大夫、蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Ni succeeded him; Ni was known from youth, and held the posts of Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes, Senior Grand Master in the Bureau of Appointments, and Governor of Cai Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ni succeeded him; Ni was known early on and held the honors of the three dukes, a senior post in the appointments bureau, and the governorship of Cai.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 嶷弟徵，從平齊，以功拜儀同大將軍，賜爵樂陵縣公。

translations.literal: Ni's younger brother Zheng followed in the pacification of Qi; for merit he was appointed General with the same honors as the Three Dukes and enfeoffed as Duke of Leling county.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's younger brother Zheng took part in conquering Qi; for merit he was made a general with the honors of the three dukes and duke of Leling.

sentences.zh: 徵弟徽，亦以軍功至儀同大將軍、保城縣男。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Hui also through military merit reached General with the same honors as the Three Dukes and Baron of Baocheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother Hui likewise rose by military merit to general with the honors of the three dukes and baron of Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 徽弟嶔，性弘厚，有局度，以齊右下大夫從武帝東伐，入并州。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Qin was by nature magnanimous and had breadth of vision; as a junior grand master of the right under Qi he followed Emperor Wu on the eastern campaign and entered Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Qin was generous and far-sighted; as a Qi official he followed Emperor Wu east, entering Bing province.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，侍臣殲焉。

translations.literal: The army was defeated and the attending officials were wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: The army was beaten and the courtiers with it were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 及帝之出，唯嶔侍從。

translations.literal: When the emperor came out, only Qin attended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor escaped, Qin alone stayed at his side.

sentences.zh: 以功授上儀同大將軍，遷開府，曆右宮伯，賜爵樂城縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Senior General with the same honors as the Three Dukes, transferred to Grand Marshal, served as Right Palace Steward, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made senior general with the honors of the three dukes, then grand marshal, served as right palace steward, and was made marquis of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位至戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Under Sui he rose to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose to minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 楊薦，字承略，秦郡寧夷人也。

translations.literal: Yang Jian, courtesy name Chenglue, was a native of Ningyi in Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian, whose courtesy name was Chenglue, came from Ningyi in Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 父寶，昌平郡守。

translations.literal: His father Bao was Administrator of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao was administrator of Changping commandery.

sentences.zh: 薦幼孤，早有名譽，性廉謹，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Jian was orphaned young, early gained a reputation, was by nature incorrupt and careful, and did not show pleasure or anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Jian won an early reputation; he was honest and restrained, and never let joy or anger show.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，隨爾硃天光入關討君賊，封高邑縣男。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era of Wei he followed Erzhu Tianguang into the passes to campaign against the emperor's rebels and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yongan era he followed Erzhu Tianguang into the passes against the emperor's rebels and was made baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 周文臨夏州，補帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took up post at Xia Province, Jian was appointed commander within the tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen went to Xia province, Jian was made a commander of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及平侯莫陳悅，使薦入洛請事，孝武授周文關西大行台，仍除薦直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue was pacified, Jian was sent to Luoyang to report affairs; Emperor Xiaowu appointed Emperor Wen Grand Commissioner of Guanxi, and at the same time made Jian Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was defeated, Jian was sent to Luoyang; Emperor Xiaowu made Emperor Wen grand commissioner of Guanxi and Jian a direct attendant general.

sentences.zh: 時馮翊長公主嫠居，孝武意欲歸諸周文，乃令武衛元毗喻旨。

translations.literal: At the time the Senior Princess of Fufeng was a widow; Emperor Xiaowu wished to give her in marriage to Emperor Wen of Zhou and therefore had the Martial Guard Yuan Pi convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The senior princess of Fufeng was then a widow; Emperor Xiaowu meant to marry her to Emperor Wen and had the guard Yuan Pi convey his wish.

sentences.zh: 薦歸白周文，又遣薦入洛陽請之，孝武即許焉。

translations.literal: Jian returned and reported to Emperor Wen, who again sent Jian to Luoyang to request her; Emperor Xiaowu at once agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian reported to Emperor Wen, who sent him again to Luoyang to ask for her hand; Emperor Xiaowu agreed at once.

sentences.zh: 孝武欲向關中，薦贊成其計。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to go to Guanzhong; Jian supported the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu wished to move to Guanzhong, Jian backed the plan.

sentences.zh: 孝武曰：「卿歸語行台迎我。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu said: "Return and tell the Commissionerate to come welcome me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu said, "Go back and tell the commissionerate to come fetch me."

sentences.zh: 周文又遣薦與長史宇文測出關候接。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou again sent Jian with Chief Clerk Yuwen Ce out of the passes to await and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen then sent Jian with chief clerk Yuwen Ce beyond the passes to receive him.

sentences.zh: 孝武至長安。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 進爵清水縣子。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Viscount of Qingshui county.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was raised to viscount of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東討，周文恐蠕蠕乘虛寇掠，乃遣薦往，更論和好，以安慰之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the great army campaigned east; Emperor Wen of Zhou feared the Rouran would seize the opportunity to raid, and therefore sent Jian to renew friendly relations and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the main army marched east; fearing Rouran raids in his absence, Emperor Wen sent Jian to renew peace and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of credentials, general of agile cavalry, and grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes, and also palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除禦伯大夫，進爵姚穀縣公，仍使突厥結婚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Jian was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Guard, advanced to Duke of Yaogu county, and again sent to arrange a marriage with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended, Jian was made grand master of the imperial guard, raised to duke of Yaogu, and again sent to arrange a marriage with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 突厥可汗弟地頭可汗阿史那庫頭居東面，與齊通和，說其兄欲背先約。

translations.literal: The Turk khagan's younger brother, the Ditou Khagan Ashina Kutou, held the east and was on good terms with Qi; he told his elder brother to break their earlier pact.
translations.idiomatic: The khan's younger brother Ashina Kutou, lord of the eastern Turks, was friendly with Qi and urged his brother to break the earlier agreement.

sentences.zh: 計謀已定，將以薦等送齊。

translations.literal: Their plot was set; they meant to send Jian and the others to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was fixed: they would hand Jian and his party over to Qi.

sentences.zh: 薦知其意，乃正色責之，辭氣慷慨，涕泗橫流。

translations.literal: Jian knew their intent and rebuked them sternly, his words impassioned and tears streaming.
translations.idiomatic: Jian saw through them and rebuked them to their faces, voice ringing and tears flowing.

sentences.zh: 可汗慘然良久曰：「幸無所疑，當共平東賊，然後發遣我女。」

translations.literal: The khagan was somber for a long while and said: "Fortunate that I have no doubts; we shall together pacify the eastern rebels, and then I will send off my daughter."
translations.idiomatic: The khan was silent a long while, then said, "You need not doubt me; we will crush the eastern rebels together, and only then will I send my daughter."

sentences.zh: 乃令薦先報命，仍請東討。

translations.literal: He then had Jian report back first and also asked to campaign east.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jian back with his answer and asked to join the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，廷大將軍。

translations.literal: Because his mission answered the court's wish, he was made Ting Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: For a mission that pleased the throne, he was made ting grand general.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，又納幣於突厥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding betrothal gifts were again sent to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding, betrothal gifts went to the Turks again.

sentences.zh: 還行小司馬，又行大司徒。

translations.literal: On his return he acted as Junior Army Marshal and then as acting Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On return he served as junior army marshal, then acting grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 從陳公純等逆女於突厥，進爵南安郡公。

translations.literal: He followed Chen Gongchun and others to escort the bride from the Turks and was advanced to Duke of Nan'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the bride from the Turks with Chen Gongchun and others and was raised to duke of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，遷總管梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he became commander-in-chief and governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥與周和親，許納女為後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Turks and Zhou made peace, they had promised to give a daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks and Zhou first made peace, they had promised a daughter for the throne.

sentences.zh: 而齊人知之，懼成合從之勢，亦遣使求婚，財饋甚厚。

translations.literal: The Qi learned of this, feared a grand alliance, and also sent envoys to ask for marriage with very rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Qi learned of it, feared a joint front, and sent envoys to propose marriage with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 突厥貪其重賂，便許之。

translations.literal: The Turks, greedy for their heavy bribes, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, tempted by the gifts, agreed.

sentences.zh: 朝議以魏氏昔與蠕蠕結婚，遂為齊人離貳，今者復恐改變，欲遣使結之。

translations.literal: Court discussion recalled that Wei once married the Rouran and Qi drove them apart; now they feared another shift and wished to send envoys to bind the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled how Wei's marriage to the Rouran had been broken by Qi and feared another switch; envoys were chosen to secure the tie.

sentences.zh: 遂授慶左武伯，副楊薦為使。

translations.literal: Qing was therefore appointed Left Martial Baron and made deputy to Yang Jian as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qing was made left martial baron and deputy to Yang Jian on the mission.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遂興入並之役。

translations.literal: That year the campaign to enter Bing was launched.
translations.idiomatic: That year the campaign into Bing was launched.

sentences.zh: 慶乃引突厥騎，與隋公楊忠至太原而還。

translations.literal: Qing then led Turk cavalry with Duke Yang Zhong of Sui to Taiyuan and back.
translations.idiomatic: Qing led Turk horsemen with Duke Yang Zhong to Taiyuan and back.

sentences.zh: 及齊人許送皇姑及世母，朝廷遂與通和。

translations.literal: When Qi agreed to send the emperor's paternal aunt and the empress dowager, the court made peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi agreed to return the imperial aunt and empress dowager, the court made peace with them.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞之，復致疑阻，於是又遣慶往諭之。

translations.literal: The Turks heard of this and again grew suspicious and obstructive; Qing was once more sent to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks heard and grew suspicious again; Qing was sent once more to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 可汗感悅，結好如初。

translations.literal: The khagan was moved and pleased; friendly relations were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was won over, and friendship was restored.

sentences.zh: 五年，復與宇文貴使突厥逆女。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again went with Yuwen Gui to escort the bride from the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again escorted the bride from the Turks with Yuwen Gui.

sentences.zh: 自此，以慶信著北蕃，頻歲出使。

translations.literal: From this Qing was trusted in the northern frontier and went on missions year after year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Qing was trusted on the northern frontier and went on missions year after year.

sentences.zh: 後更至突厥，屬其可汗暴殂，突厥謂慶曰：「前後使來，逢我國喪者，皆緌面表哀。

translations.literal: Later he again reached the Turks; their khagan had suddenly died. The Turks said to Qing: "Envoys before and after, when they met our national mourning, all wore mourning veils to show grief.
translations.idiomatic: On a later mission the Turk khan died suddenly. The Turks told Qing, "Every envoy who came during our mourning wore a mourning veil.

sentences.zh: 況今二國和親，豈得不行此事！」

translations.literal: Moreover, now the two states are kin by marriage—how can you not do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Now our houses are joined by marriage—how can you refuse!

sentences.zh: 慶抗辭不從。

translations.literal: Qing refused firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Qing refused outright.

sentences.zh: 突厥見其守正，卒不敢逼，武帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The Turks, seeing his integrity, did not dare compel him in the end; Emperor Wu heard and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his steadfastness, the Turks did not dare force him; Emperor Wu praised him when he heard.

sentences.zh: 錄慶前後使功，遷開府儀同三司、兵部中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Recording Qing's services on his many missions, he was made Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes and Senior Grand Master in the Ministry of War, and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated missions were rewarded with the honors of the three dukes, a senior war ministry post, and a ducal title.

sentences.zh: 曆丹、中二州刺史，為政嚴肅，吏不敢犯。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Dan and Zhong provinces; his government was stern and officials did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Dan and Zhong he ruled sternly and officials did not dare cross him.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，授小司徒，加上大將軍、總管汾石二州五鎮諸軍事、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang he was appointed Junior Minister of Education, with additional titles of Senior Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for five garrisons of Fen and Shi provinces and Governor of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he became junior minister of education, senior grand general, and commander over Fen and Shi with five garrisons.

sentences.zh: 又除延州總管，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was also made Commander-in-Chief of Yan Province and advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made commander of Yan and raised to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進爵平昌郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang his rank was advanced to Duke of Pingchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was raised to duke of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮，贈上柱國，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He died in his command; posthumously he was made Supreme Pillar of State with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died on duty and was posthumously made supreme pillar of state with the name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子淹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 趙剛，字僧慶，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Gang, courtesy name Sengqing, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gang, whose courtesy name was Sengqing, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖甯，魏高平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ning was Governor of Gaoping under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ning had been governor of Gaoping under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父和，永平中，陵江將軍。

translations.literal: His father He, in the Yongping era, was General Who Crosses the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His father He had been general who crosses the Yangzi in the Yongping era.

sentences.zh: 南討度淮，聞父喪，輒還，所司將致之於法，和曰：「罔極之恩，終天莫報。

translations.literal: Campaigning south he crossed the Huai; hearing of his father's death he turned back, and the authorities were about to punish him by law. He said: "The utmost of filial debt can never be repaid in a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: On a southern campaign he crossed the Huai; when he heard his father had died he turned back, and the authorities meant to punish him. He said, "A son's debt to his father can never be fully paid.

sentences.zh: 若許安厝，禮畢而即罪戮，死且無恨。

translations.literal: If I may bury him in peace, I will accept punishment after the rites are done and die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Let me bury him properly; after the rites you may execute me, and I will die without regret.

sentences.zh: 言訖號慟，悲感傍人。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he wailed aloud, moving those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: He ended with a wail that moved everyone nearby.

sentences.zh: 主司以聞，遂宥之。

translations.literal: The presiding official reported it, and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The officer reported upward, and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 喪畢，除甯遠將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed General of Tranquil Distance.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made general of tranquil distance.

sentences.zh: 大統初，追贈膠州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong his father was posthumously made Governor of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong his father was posthumously made governor of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 剛少機辯，有幹能，起家奉朝請，累遷金紫光祿大夫，領司徒府從事中郎，加閣內都督。

translations.literal: Gang in youth was quick and resourceful with practical ability; he began as Court Attendant and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, served as Attendant in the Ministry of Education, and was made Commander within the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was sharp and capable from youth; he rose from court attendant to grand master of splendid virtue, served in the education ministry, and became an inner-gate commander.

sentences.zh: 及孝武與齊神武構隙，剛密奉旨，召東荊州刺史馮景昭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu fell out with Gao Huan of Qi, Gang secretly received orders to summon Feng Jingzhao, Governor of Eastern Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu broke with Gao Huan of Qi, Gang secretly received orders to summon Feng Jingzhao, governor of eastern Jing.

sentences.zh: 未及發，而神武已逼洛陽，孝武西遷。

translations.literal: Before he could set out, Huan had already pressed on Luoyang and Xiaowu moved west.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could act, Huan was already at Luoyang and Xiaowu fled west.

sentences.zh: 景昭集府僚文武，議其去就，司馬馮道和請據州待北方處分。

translations.literal: Jingzhao gathered civil and military officials to decide whether to stay or go; his marshal Feng Daohe asked to hold the province and await the north's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao gathered his staff to decide their course; his marshal Feng Daohe urged holding the province and waiting on the north.

sentences.zh: 剛抽刀投地曰：「公若為忠臣，可斬道和。

translations.literal: Gang drew his sword and cast it to the ground, saying: "If you mean to be a loyal minister, you can kill Daohe.
translations.idiomatic: Gang threw his sword to the ground: "If you are loyal, kill Daohe.

sentences.zh: 如欲從賊，可見殺！」

translations.literal: If you wish to follow the rebels, you may kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to join the rebels, kill me instead!

sentences.zh: 景昭感悟，遂率眾赴關右。

translations.literal: Jingzhao was moved and led his forces to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao was stirred and led his men west to Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景逼穰城，東荊州人楊歡等起兵應景，以其眾邀景昭于路。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing pressed Xiangcheng, the people of Eastern Jing under Yang Huan and others rose for Jing and intercepted Jingzhao on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged Xiangcheng, Yang Huan and others of eastern Jing rose for Jing and blocked Jingzhao on the road.

sentences.zh: 景昭戰敗，剛遂沒於蠻。

translations.literal: Jingzhao was defeated and Gang was taken by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao was beaten and Gang fell into tribal hands.

sentences.zh: 後自贖免，乃見東魏東荊州刺史李魔憐，勸令歸關西。

translations.literal: Later he ransomed himself and saw Li Molian, Eastern Jing Governor under Eastern Wei, and urged him to return to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later ransomed himself, saw Li Molian of Eastern Wei, and urged him west.

sentences.zh: 魔憐納之，使剛至并州，密觀事勢。

translations.literal: Molian accepted this and sent Gang to Bing Province to observe affairs secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Molian agreed and sent Gang to Bing to watch affairs.

sentences.zh: 神武引剛內宴，因令剛賚書申敕荊州。

translations.literal: Huan entertained Gang at a private banquet and had him carry a letter with orders to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huan feasted Gang privately and gave him a letter for Jing province.

sentences.zh: 剛還報魔憐，仍說魔憐斬楊歡等，以州歸西。

translations.literal: Gang reported back to Molian and also urged him to kill Yang Huan and surrender the province west.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reported to Molian and urged him to kill Yang Huan and surrender the province.

sentences.zh: 魔憐乃使剛入朝。

translations.literal: Molian then sent Gang to court.
translations.idiomatic: Molian then sent Gang to court.

sentences.zh: 大統初，剛於灞上見周文，具陳關東情實。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Gang met Emperor Wen of Zhou at Bashang and fully reported conditions east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong Gang met Emperor Wen at Bashang and laid out the situation east of the passes.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，封陽邑縣子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was pleased and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Yangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was pleased and made him viscount of Yangyi.

sentences.zh: 論復東荊州功，進爵臨汝縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit in recovering Eastern Jing Province his rank was advanced to Baron of Linru county.
translations.idiomatic: For recovering eastern Jing he was raised to baron of Linru.

sentences.zh: 初，賀拔勝、獨孤信以孝武西遷之後，並流寓江左。

translations.literal: Earlier, Heba Sheng and Dugu Xin, after Xiaowu's move west, had both been stranded in the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Sheng and Dugu Xin had been stranded south of the Yangzi after Xiaowu went west.

sentences.zh: 至是，剛言于魏文帝，請追而復之。

translations.literal: Now Gang spoke to Emperor Wen of Wei, asking that they be summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Gang now asked Emperor Wen of Wei to bring them back.

sentences.zh: 乃以剛為兼給事黃門侍郎，使梁魏興，賚移書與其梁州刺史杜懷寶等。

translations.literal: Gang was therefore made Acting Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent to Liang's Weixing with a letter for their Governor Du Huaibao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting yellow-gate attendant and sent to Liang's Weixing with letters for Du Huaibao and others.

sentences.zh: 即與剛盟歃，受移送建康，仍遣人隨剛報命。

translations.literal: They at once swore alliance with Gang, received the letter for Jiankang, and sent men back with him to report.
translations.idiomatic: They swore alliance with him, sent the letter to Jiankang, and returned envoys with him.

sentences.zh: 是年，又詔剛使三荊，聽在所便宜從事。

translations.literal: That year an edict also sent Gang to the three Jing regions with authority to act as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was also sent to the three Jing regions with discretionary power.

sentences.zh: 使還，稱旨，進爵武成縣侯，除大丞相府帳內都督。

translations.literal: When the mission returned it pleased the throne; his rank was advanced to Marquis of Wucheng county and he was made Commander within the Grand Chancellor's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His mission pleased the throne; he was made marquis of Wucheng and commander in the grand chancellor's guard.

sentences.zh: 復使魏興，重申前命。

translations.literal: He was again sent to Weixing to renew the earlier charge.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent again to Weixing to renew the earlier charge.

sentences.zh: 尋而梁人禮送賀拔勝、獨孤信等。

translations.literal: Before long Liang courteously sent back Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liang courteously returned Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and the others.

sentences.zh: 頃之，御史中尉董紹進策，請圖梁漢，以紹為行台、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long the Censor-in-Chief Dong Shao proposed a plan to take Liang's Han region; Shao was made Commissioner and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censor Dong Shao proposed taking Liang's Han; Shao was made commissioner and governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 剛以為不可，而朝議已決，遂出軍。

translations.literal: Gang thought it unwise, but the court had decided and the army went out.
translations.idiomatic: Gang thought it unwise, but the court had decided and the army marched.

sentences.zh: 紹竟無功還，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Shao returned without success and was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Shao failed and was reduced to commoner.

sentences.zh: 除剛潁州郡守。

translations.literal: Gang was appointed Administrator of Yingzhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was made administrator of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州來附，兼大行台左丞，持節赴潁川節度義軍。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi came over with Beiyu Province, Gang was made concurrently Left Assistant of the Grand Commissionerate with credentials to coordinate the loyal armies at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi defected with Beiyu, Gang was left assistant commissioner with authority at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 師還，剛別破侯景前驅于南陸，復獲其郡守二人。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Gang separately defeated Hou Jing's vanguard at Nanlu and also captured two of his commandery administrators.
translations.idiomatic: On the return Gang beat Hou Jing's vanguard at Nanlu and took two of his administrators.

sentences.zh: 時有流言，傳剛東叛，神武因設反間，聲遣迎接。

translations.literal: At the time rumor spread that Gang had defected east; Huan therefore set up a stratagem, pretending to send men to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor then spread that Gang had defected east; Huan staged a false welcome.

sentences.zh: 剛乃率騎襲其丁塢，拔之，周文知剛無貳，乃加賚焉。

translations.literal: Gang then led horsemen in a raid on their camp and took it; Emperor Wen knew Gang was loyal and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gang raided their camp and took it; Emperor Wen knew he was loyal and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 除營州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Ying Province and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Ying and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 渭州人鄭五醜構逆，與叛羌傍乞鐵勿相應。

translations.literal: Zheng Wuchou of Wei Province raised rebellion in concert with the rebel Qiang Pangqi Tiewu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wuchou of Wei rebelled alongside the Qiang Pangqi Tiewu.

sentences.zh: 令剛往鎮之。

translations.literal: Gang was ordered to go and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was ordered to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 將發，魏文帝引見內寢，舉觴屬剛曰：「昔侯景在東，為卿所困。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Emperor Wen of Wei received him in the inner quarters, raised a cup, and charged Gang: "In former days Hou Jing in the east was trapped by you.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Emperor Wen received him privately, raised a cup, and said, "Hou Jing in the east was once trapped by you.

sentences.zh: 黠羌小丑，豈足勞卿謀慮也？」

translations.literal: These cunning Qiang bandits—are they worth your planning?"
translations.idiomatic: Are these sly Qiang rabble worth your trouble?

sentences.zh: 時五醜已克定夷鎮，所在立柵。

translations.literal: By then Wuchou had already taken Yizhen; stockades were set up everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchou had already taken Yizhen and fortified every strong point.

sentences.zh: 剛至，並攻破之，散其黨與。

translations.literal: When Gang arrived he broke them all and dispersed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Gang broke them one by one and scattered their bands.

sentences.zh: 五醜於是西奔鐵勿，剛又進破鐵勿偽廣寧郡。

translations.literal: Wuchou then fled west to Tiewu; Gang advanced and destroyed Tiewu's false Guangning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchou fled west to Tiewu; Gang destroyed Tiewu's sham Guangning commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬宇文貴等西討，詔以剛行渭州事，資給糧餼。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Gui and others campaigned west, an edict had Gang act for Wei Province affairs and supply grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Gui marched west, Gang was ordered to run Wei province and supply grain.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，入為光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was made General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal with the same honors as the Three Dukes and entered as Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of agile cavalry, grand marshal with the honors of the three dukes, and minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜膳部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Senior Grand Master in the Commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were set up he became senior grand master of the commissariat.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進爵浮陽郡公，出為利州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Gang was advanced to Duke of Fuyang commandery and went out as Commander-in-Chief of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended, Gang was raised to duke of Fuyang and made commander of Li.

sentences.zh: 沙州氐恃險逆命，剛再討復之。

translations.literal: The Di of Sha Province relied on terrain and defied orders; Gang campaigned twice and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Sha defied the court; Gang subdued them twice.

sentences.zh: 方州生獠，自此始從賦役。

translations.literal: The raw tribes of Fang Province from this time began to pay tax and corvée.
