translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Fang from then on paid tax and labor.

sentences.zh: 剛以信州濱江負阻，乃表請討之。

translations.literal: Gang, because Xin Province lay along the river behind difficult barriers, memorialized asking to campaign there.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin lay along the river behind barriers, he asked to campaign there.

sentences.zh: 詔剛率利、沙等十四州兵往經略焉。

translations.literal: An edict had Gang lead troops of fourteen provinces including Li and Sha to conduct operations.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead troops from fourteen provinces including Li and Sha.

sentences.zh: 仍加授渠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Governor of Qu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made governor of Qu.

sentences.zh: 剛初至，梁帥憚其軍威，相次降款。

translations.literal: When Gang first arrived, Liang commanders feared his army and surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Liang commanders feared him and surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 剛師出逾年，士卒疲弊，尋復亡叛。

translations.literal: After Gang had been in the field more than a year, his soldiers were worn out and soon rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his men were exhausted and rebellion returned.

sentences.zh: 後遂以入功而還。

translations.literal: He later returned on account of merit in entering.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned citing merit from the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又與所部儀同尹才失和，被徵赴闕，遇疾，卒于路。

translations.literal: He also fell out with his subordinate Yitong Yin Cai, was summoned to court, fell ill on the road, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with his subordinate Yin Cai, was recalled, fell ill on the road, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈中、淅、涿三州刺史，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Governor of Zhong, Xi, and Zhuo provinces, with the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Zhong, Xi, and Zhuo, with the name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子元卿，弟仲卿。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqing and younger brother Zhongqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanqing and younger brother Zhongqing.

sentences.zh: 仲卿性粗暴，有膂力。

translations.literal: Zhongqing was rough by nature and had great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing was rough by nature and immensely strong.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲甚禮之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi of Zhou, Yuwen Xian, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi under the Zhou, honored him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 以軍功位上儀同，為畿伯中大夫。

translations.literal: By military merit he attained the rank of Upper Yitong and served as Jibo Central Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: For his battlefield achievements he was made Upper Yitong and appointed Jibo Central Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 後以平王謙功，進位大將軍，封長垣縣公。

translations.literal: Later, for his merit in suppressing Prince of Ping Yuwen Qian, he was advanced to Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his role in putting down Yuwen Qian, Prince of Ping, he was promoted to Grand General and created Duke of Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進河北郡公，尋拜石州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was advanced to Duke of Hebei commandery; soon afterward he was appointed governor of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Zhongqing was raised to Duke of Hebei and soon named governor of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 法令嚴猛，纖介之失無所寬舍，鞭笞輒至二百。

translations.literal: His laws and orders were stern and harsh; the slightest fault found no indulgence, and flogging often reached two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law with pitiless severity: no trifling lapse went unpunished, and beatings routinely ran to two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 吏人戰慄無敢違犯，盜賊屏息，皆稱其能。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners trembled in fear and dared not violate him; bandits fell silent, and all praised his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and people alike shrank from defying him, brigandage died away, and everyone acclaimed his effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 遷朔州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be area commander of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to the post of area commander of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時塞北盛興屯田，仲卿總統之。

translations.literal: At that time the northern frontier greatly promoted military colonies, and Zhongqing oversaw them all.
translations.idiomatic: Military farming was then being pushed hard along the northern marches, and Zhongqing directed the whole effort.

sentences.zh: 微有不理者，仲卿輒召主掌撻其胸背，或解衣倒曳於荊棘中，時人謂之於菟。

translations.literal: Where anything was the least irregular, Zhongqing would summon the responsible officer and flog his chest and back, or strip him and drag him backward through brambles; contemporaries called him a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest irregularity he had the supervisor beaten on chest and back, or stripped and hauled backward through thorn scrub—so people nicknamed him "the tiger."

sentences.zh: 事多克濟，由是收穫歲廣，邊戍無饋運之憂。

translations.literal: Matters mostly succeeded; thereby the harvest grew year by year, and the border garrisons had no worry of supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: Most projects succeeded; harvests swelled year after year, and frontier posts no longer feared running short of supplies.

sentences.zh: 會突厥啟人可汗求婚，上許之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Türk Qiren Qaghan sought a marriage alliance, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk Qiren Qaghan asked for a marriage alliance, the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 仲卿因是間其骨肉，遂相攻擊。

translations.literal: Zhongqing thereby sowed discord among their kin, and they came to attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing used the occasion to set their kin against one another until they were fighting among themselves.

sentences.zh: 十七年，啟人窘迫，與隋使長孫晟投通漢鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Qiren was hard pressed and, with the Sui envoy Zhangsun Sheng, fled to throw themselves on Tonghan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, Qiren, brought to bay, fled with the Sui envoy Zhangsun Sheng to seek refuge at Tonghan Fort.

sentences.zh: 仲卿率騎千餘援之，達頭不敢逼。

translations.literal: Zhongqing led more than a thousand horsemen to relieve them; Datou did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing rode out with over a thousand cavalry to rescue them, and Datou did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 潛遣人誘致啟人所部，至者二萬餘家。

translations.literal: He secretly sent men to entice Qiren's following; those who came numbered more than twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent agents to lure away Qiren's tribesmen, and more than twenty thousand families came over.

sentences.zh: 其年，從高熲指白道以擊達頭，仲卿為前鋒。

translations.literal: That year, following Gao Jiong toward the White Road to strike Datou, Zhongqing served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he followed Gao Jiong along the White Road against Datou, serving as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至族蠡山，與虜遇，交戰七日，大破之。

translations.literal: Reaching Zuluo Mountain, they met the barbarians; after seven days of battle they inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuluo Mountain they met the enemy; after seven days of fighting they shattered the Türk force.

sentences.zh: 追奔至乞伏泊，復啟人。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives to Qifu Marsh, they restored Qiren.
translations.idiomatic: They chased the fugitives to Qifu Marsh and restored Qiren to power.

sentences.zh: 突厥悉眾而至，仲卿為方陣，四面拒戰，經五日。

translations.literal: The Türks came in full strength; Zhongqing formed a square array and resisted on four sides for five days.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks arrived in full strength; Zhongqing drew up a square formation and held them on every side for five days.

sentences.zh: 會高熲大兵至，合擊之，虜乃敗走。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong's great army arrived; joining forces they struck, and the barbarians then fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong's main force arrived they attacked together and drove the enemy off in rout.

sentences.zh: 追度白道，逾秦山七百餘里。

translations.literal: The pursuit crossed the White Road and went beyond Qin Mountain for more than seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit crossed the White Road and pressed more than seven hundred li beyond Qin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時突厥降者萬餘家，上令仲卿處之恆安。

translations.literal: At that time Türks who surrendered numbered more than ten thousand households; the emperor ordered Zhongqing to settle them at Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Türk households had surrendered; the emperor had Zhongqing resettle them at Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 以功進上柱國。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to Upper Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was promoted to Upper Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮達頭掩襲啟人，令仲卿屯兵二萬以備之，代州總管韓洪、永康公李藥王、蔚州刺史劉隆等將步騎一萬鎮恆安，達頭來寇，韓洪軍大敗。

translations.literal: The court feared Datou might launch a surprise attack on Qiren and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in readiness; the Shuozhou area commander Han Hong, the Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, the governor of Yu Prefecture Liu Long, and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an; Datou came to raid and Han Hong's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Datou might swoop on Qiren, the court ordered Zhongqing to hold twenty thousand men in reserve; Han Hong, area commander of Dai, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, governor of Yu, and others took ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Heng'an—yet when Datou attacked, Han Hong's force was crushed.

sentences.zh: 仲鄉自樂寧鎮邀擊，斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang from Leling Fort launched an intercepting attack and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From Leling Fort, Zhongqing struck in interception and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，督役築金河、定襄二城以居啟人。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised labor to build the Jinhe and Dingxiang cities to house Qiren.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he oversaw construction of the Jinhe and Dingxiang walled towns to settle Qiren's people.

sentences.zh: 時有上表言仲卿酷暴，上命御史王偉按之，並實。

translations.literal: At that time someone memorialized that Zhongqing was cruel and violent; the emperor ordered the censor Wang Wei to investigate, and all was found true.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then memorialized that Zhongqing was brutal; the emperor sent the censor Wang Wei to investigate, and every charge proved true.

sentences.zh: 惜其功，不罪，因勞之曰：「知公清正，為下所惡。」

translations.literal: Pitying his merit, he was not punished; instead the emperor comforted him, saying: "I know you are upright and clear, and are hated by your subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared him out of regard for his service and comforted him: "I know you are upright—and that your subordinates hate you for it.

sentences.zh: 賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred bolts of goods as a reward.

sentences.zh: 仲卿益恣，由是免官。

translations.literal: Zhongqing became all the more unrestrained; thereby he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing grew only more overbearing, and for that he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，檢校司農卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was made acting Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Renshou reign he was appointed acting Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪，奉詔往益州按之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu, Yang Xiu, fell into guilt, he received an edict to go to Yizhou to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shu Yang Xiu was implicated, Zhongqing was ordered to Yizhou to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 秀賓客經過處，仲卿必深文致法，州縣長吏坐者太半。

translations.literal: Wherever Xiu's retainers had passed, Zhongqing invariably twisted the law to the utmost; prefectural and county chief officials implicated numbered more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yang Xiu's clients had been, Zhongqing stretched the law to its harshest limit, and well over half the prefectural and county heads were punished.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，賞奴婢五十口、黃金二百兩、米粟五千石、奇寶雜物稱是。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable and rewarded him with fifty slaves and maidservants, two hundred taels of gold, five thousand shi of grain, and rare treasures and miscellaneous goods in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him capable and rewarded him with fifty bondsmen and maidservants, two hundred taels of gold, five thousand shi of grain, and a comparable trove of curios and valuables.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，判兵部、工部二尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was assigned to adjudicate the affairs of the two ministries of War and Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Zhongqing was put in charge of the ministries of War and of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title is Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous epithet was Su.

sentences.zh: 子世弘嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shihong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihong inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 趙昶，字長舒，天水南安人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang, style name Changshu, was a man of Nan'an in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang, courtesy name Changshu, came from Nan'an in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖襄，仕魏，至中山郡守，因家於代焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiang served Wei and reached governor of Zhongshan commandery; he then made his home in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiang had served the Wei and risen to governor of Zhongshan, then settled his family in Dai.

sentences.zh: 昶少聰敏，有志節。

translations.literal: Chang in youth was clever and keen, with will and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhao Chang was quick-witted and resolute.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，以材力聞。

translations.literal: At weak cap age he became known for physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: By his coming of age he was famed for strength and courage.

sentences.zh: 魏北中郎將高千鎮陝，以昶為長史、中軍都督。

translations.literal: Gao Qian, North Zhonglang General of Wei, garrisoned Shan; he made Chang his chief clerk and Central Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei North Zhonglang General Gao Qian held Shan, he made Chang his chief clerk and Central Army commander.

sentences.zh: 周文平弘農，擢為相府典簽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou pacified Hongnong, he was promoted to be the chancellor's office registry clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Zhou took Hongnong, Zhao Chang was raised to registry clerk in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，大軍失律於芒山，清水氐酋李鼠仁自軍逃還，憑險作亂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong, the great army lost discipline at Mangshan; the Qingshui Di chieftain Li Shuren fled from the army back home and, relying on rugged terrain, raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year nine the main force broke discipline at Mangshan; the Qingshui Di chieftain Li Shuren deserted, returned home, and rebelled from the highlands.

sentences.zh: 周文將討之，先求可使者，遂令昶使焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou was about to campaign against him and first sought someone who could be sent; he then ordered Chang to go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou prepared to suppress him and first asked who could be sent as envoy; he chose Zhao Chang.

sentences.zh: 見鼠仁，喻以禍福。

translations.literal: Seeing Shuren, he explained fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang confronted Shuren and laid out the consequences of resistance and submission.

sentences.zh: 群凶或從或不，從其命者，復將加刃於昶。

translations.literal: Among the ringleaders some obeyed and some did not; those who obeyed his command were again about to put blades to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the chiefs agreed and some refused; even those inclined to obey still threatened to kill him.

sentences.zh: 而昶神色自若，志氣彌厲。

translations.literal: Yet Chang's expression was calm as ever, and his spirit grew all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao Chang's face stayed calm and his resolve only hardened.

sentences.zh: 鼠仁感悟，遂相率降。

translations.literal: Shuren was moved to understanding and then led one another in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuren was moved, and the Di submitted in a body.

sentences.zh: 氐梁道顯叛，攻南由，周文復遣昶慰喻之，道顯等皆即款附。

translations.literal: The Di Liang Daoxian rebelled and attacked Nanyou; Emperor Wen of Zhou again sent Chang to console and persuade them, and Daoxian and the rest at once came to sincere submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di leader Liang Daoxian rebelled and attacked Nanyou, Emperor Wen of Zhou again sent Zhao Chang to win them over, and Daoxian and his fellows promptly submitted.

sentences.zh: 東秦州刺史魏光因徙其豪帥三十餘人並部落于華州，周文即以昶為都督領之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Qinzhou governor Wei Guang had earlier moved more than thirty of their great chiefs together with their tribes to Huazhou; Emperor Wen of Zhou then made Chang commander to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Qinzhou governor Wei Guang had earlier relocated more than thirty Di chiefs with their clans to Huazhou; Emperor Wen of Zhou now put Zhao Chang in command of them.

sentences.zh: 先是，汾州胡叛，再遣昶慰勞之，皆知其虛實。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hu of Fenzhou had rebelled; Chang was twice sent to console and comfort them, and he came to know their true situation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu of Fen had rebelled earlier, Zhao Chang was twice sent to reassure them and learned their real strength.

sentences.zh: 及大軍往討，昶為先驅，遂破之。

translations.literal: When the great army went to campaign, Chang served as vanguard and thereupon broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched out, he led the van and broke them.

sentences.zh: 以功封章武縣伯。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu county.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was created Baron of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜安夷郡守，帶長蛇鎮將。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor of Anyi commandery, concurrently commander of Changshe Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he was made governor of Anyi and concurrently commander of Changshe Fort.

sentences.zh: 氐俗荒獷，昶威懷以禮，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Di custom was wild and fierce; Chang awed and embraced them with ritual, and none failed to submit gladly.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were a rough people; Zhao Chang ruled them with stern ceremony and gentle regard until all were glad to obey.

sentences.zh: 期歲之後，樂從軍者千餘人。

translations.literal: After the space of a year, more than a thousand were glad to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year more than a thousand volunteered for military service.

sentences.zh: 加授帥都督。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted the title of commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時屬軍機，科發切急，氐情難之，復相率謀叛。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs pressed and levies were urgent; the Di found it hard to bear, and again they plotted rebellion together.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime levies then grew crushing; the Di rebelled again in concert.

sentences.zh: 昶又潛遣誘說，離間其情。

translations.literal: Chang again secretly sent men to entice and persuade, sundering their sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang again sent secret emissaries to sow division among them.

sentences.zh: 因其攜貳，遂輕往臨之。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their divided loyalties, he then went lightly to face them in person.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting their wavering loyalty, he went in person with only a light escort.

sentences.zh: 群氐不知所為，咸來見昶，乃收其首逆者二十餘人斬之，餘眾遂定。

translations.literal: The Di masses did not know what to do; all came to see Chang; he then seized the chief ringleaders, more than twenty men, and beheaded them, and the rest were thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di did not know which way to turn; they all came before Zhao Chang, who seized and executed more than twenty ringleaders, and the rest quieted down.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，除大都督，行南秦州事。

translations.literal: The court praised this and appointed him Grand Commander, acting for Southern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him, made him Grand Commander, and put him in charge of Southern Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時氐帥蓋鬧等反，昶復討禽之。

translations.literal: At that time the Di chieftain Gai Nao and others rebelled; Chang again campaigned and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di chieftain Gai Nao rebelled, Zhao Chang campaigned again and took him.

sentences.zh: 又與史寧破宕昌羌、獠二十餘萬。

translations.literal: He also with Shi Ning broke the Dangchang Qiang and Liao, more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Ning he also defeated more than two hundred thousand Dangchang Qiang and Liao.

sentences.zh: 拜武州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Gongdi reign he was added Grand General Agile as Tiger and Director of the Office with the Third Rank of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the accession of Emperor Gong he was made Grand General Agile as Tiger with the third rank of court honor.

sentences.zh: 潭水羌叛，殺武陵、潭水二郡守。

translations.literal: The Tanshui Qiang rebelled and killed the governors of Wuling and Tanshui commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanshui Qiang rebelled and killed the governors of Wuling and Tanshui.

sentences.zh: 昶率儀同駱天人等討平之。

translations.literal: Chang led the Yitong Luo Tianren and others to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang led Luo Tianren, an officer of Yitong rank, and others to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，鳳州人仇周貢、魏興等反，自號周公，破廣化郡，攻沒諸縣，分兵西入，圍廣業、脩城二郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou, the men of Fengzhou, Qiu Zhougong and Wei Xing, rebelled, styled themselves Duke of Zhou, broke Guanghua commandery, and overran the counties; they divided troops to enter westward and besieged the two commanderies of Guangye and Xiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign, Qiu Zhougong and Wei Xing of Fengzhou rebelled, proclaimed themselves Duke of Zhou, stormed Guanghua commandery, overran the counties, and sent a column west to besiege Guangye and Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 廣業郡守薛爽、脩城郡守杜杲等請昶為援。

translations.literal: The governors of Guangye and Xiucheng, Xue Shuang and Du Guo, requested Chang as relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shuang, governor of Guangye, and Du Guo of Xiucheng asked Zhao Chang for aid.

sentences.zh: 遣使報杲，為周貢党樊伏興等所獲。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to report to Guo, but the messenger was seized by Zhougong's party, Fan Fuxing and others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a courier to Du Guo, but Zhougong's adherent Fan Fuxing intercepted him.

sentences.zh: 興等知昶將至，解脩城圍，據泥功嶺，設六伏以待昶。

translations.literal: Fuxing and the rest, knowing Chang was about to arrive, lifted the siege of Xiucheng and held Nigong Ridge, setting six ambushes to await Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhao Chang was coming, Fuxing lifted the siege of Xiucheng, took Nigong Ridge, and laid six ambushes.

sentences.zh: 昶至，遂遇其伏，合戰破之。

translations.literal: When Chang arrived he thereupon met their ambush; joining battle he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang walked into the trap, fought, and broke it.

sentences.zh: 廣業之圍亦解，昶追之至泥陽川而還。

translations.literal: The siege of Guangye was also lifted; Chang pursued to Niyang River and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Guangye lifted as well; he pursued to the Niyang River and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興州人段吒及氐酋薑多復反，攻沒郡縣，昶討斬之。

translations.literal: The men of Xingzhou, Duan Tuo, and the Di chieftain Jiang Duo again rebelled and overran commanderies and counties; Chang campaigned and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Tuo of Xingzhou and the Di chieftain Jiang Duo rebelled again and seized districts; Zhao Chang campaigned and executed them.

sentences.zh: 昶自以被拔擢居將帥之任，傾心下士，虜獲氐、羌，撫而使之，皆為昶盡力。

translations.literal: Chang considered himself pulled up to bear a commander's charge; he devoted his heart to men below; captives among the Di and Qiang he embraced and employed, and all exerted their strength for Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had been lifted from obscurity to high command, he devoted himself to his men; Di and Qiang prisoners he won over, and all fought wholeheartedly for him.

sentences.zh: 周文常曰：「不煩國家士馬而能威服氐、羌者，趙昶有之矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou often said: "Without troubling the state's soldiers and horses yet able to awe and subdue the Di and Qiang—Zhao Chang has this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou often said, "To awe the Di and Qiang without spending the state's troops—only Zhao Chang can do that.

sentences.zh: 至是，明帝錄前後功，進爵長道郡公，賜姓宇文氏，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Ming recorded his former and later merit, advanced his noble rank to Duke of Changdao commandery, granted the surname Yuwen, and rewarded and comforted him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming now tallied his past and recent service, raised him to Duke of Changdao, granted the surname Yuwen, and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵拜賓部中大夫，行吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned and appointed Guest Department Central Grand Master, acting for the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was recalled as Guest Department Central Grand Master with acting charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 王悅，字眾喜，京兆藍田人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yue, style name Zhongxi, was a man of Lantian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, courtesy name Zhongxi, was from Lantian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹，為州裏所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and backbone and was praised by his district.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he had force of character, and his home district spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 周文初定關隴，悅率募鄉里從軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first secured Guan and Long, Yue led men he had recruited from his home district into the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first secured the Guan-Long region, Wang Yue mustered neighbors and joined the army.

sentences.zh: 屢有戰功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly had military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He won distinction again and again in battle.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，除相府刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was made Criminal Punishments Aide in the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year one he became Criminal Punishments Aide in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 封藍田縣伯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Lantian county.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Baron of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 四年，東魏將侯景攻圍洛陽，周文赴援，悅又率鄉里千餘人從軍至洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Eastern Wei general Hou Jing besieged Luoyang; Emperor Wen of Zhou went to relieve it, and Yue again led more than a thousand men of his home district in the army to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, when Hou Jing of Eastern Wei besieged Luoyang, Emperor Wen of Zhou marched to relieve the city and Wang Yue again brought more than a thousand local men to the front.

sentences.zh: 將戰之夕，悅罄其行資，市牛饗戰士。

translations.literal: On the eve of battle Yue spent all his traveling funds to buy oxen and feast the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle he spent his entire travel purse buying oxen to feast his troops.

sentences.zh: 悅所部盡力。

translations.literal: The troops under Yue exerted their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The men under his command fought with everything they had.

sentences.zh: 斬獲居多。

translations.literal: Beheadings and captures were mostly his.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the kills and captures fell to his unit.

sentences.zh: 遷大行台右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Great Expeditionary Office, then transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Great Expeditionary Office, then to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 久居管轄，頗獲時譽。

translations.literal: Long holding supervisory office, he gained considerable contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Long in high administrative posts, he earned a solid reputation at court.

sentences.zh: 十三年，侯景據河南來附，仍請兵為援，周文先遣韋法保、賀蘭願德等帥眾助之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing held Henan and came to submit; he still requested troops as aid; Emperor Wen of Zhou first sent Wei Fabao, Helan Yuande, and others to lead troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen Hou Jing, holding Henan, defected and asked for reinforcements; Emperor Wen of Zhou first sent Wei Fabao, Helan Yuande, and others to help him.

sentences.zh: 悅言于周文曰：「侯景之于高歡，始則篤鄉黨之情，末乃定君臣之契，位居上將，職重台司，論其分義，有同魚水。

translations.literal: Yue spoke to Emperor Wen of Zhou, saying: "Hou Jing toward Gao Huan at first had the affection of fellow townsmen, and in the end fixed the bond of lord and minister; his position was top general, his office weighty as Grand Secretary; speaking of their share of duty, they were like fish and water.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue told Emperor Wen of Zhou, "Hou Jing and Gao Huan began as fellow townsmen and ended as lord and minister; he was a top general with duties as weighty as a Grand Secretary's—together they were like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 今歡始死，景便離貳，豈不知君臣之道有違，忠義之禮不足？

translations.literal: Now Huan has just died and Jing at once turns disloyal—does he not know that the way of lord and minister is violated and the ritual of loyalty and righteousness is insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Now that Huan has just died, Jing turns traitor at once—does he not see that he is trampling the bond between lord and minister and abandoning loyalty and righteousness?

sentences.zh: 蓋其圖既大，不恤小嫌。

translations.literal: His design is already great and he does not spare small resentments.
translations.idiomatic: His ambitions are large; he will not trouble himself over lesser slights.

sentences.zh: 然尚能背德于高氏，豈肯盡節於朝廷？

translations.literal: Yet if he can turn his back on virtue toward the Gao clan, how can he exhaust his devotion to the court?
translations.idiomatic: If he could betray the Gao family, how could he give his full loyalty to our court?

sentences.zh: 今若益之以勢，援之以兵，非唯侯景不為池中之物，亦恐朝廷貽笑將來也。」

translations.literal: Now if you further add power and send troops in support, not only will Hou Jing not remain a fish in the pool, but I fear the court will also be laughed at by posterity.
translations.idiomatic: If we now add to his strength and send him troops, Hou Jing will not stay a fish in the pond—and our court will be mocked by posterity.

sentences.zh: 周文納之，乃遣追法保等，而景尋叛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou accepted this and then sent to recall Fabao and the rest, and Jing soon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou took his advice and recalled Wei Fabao and the others; Hou Jing soon rebelled anyway.

sentences.zh: 後拜京兆郡守、散騎常侍，遷大行台尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed governor of Jingzhao commandery and Regular Attendant, and moved to Director of the Great Expeditionary Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Jingzhao and Regular Attendant, then Director of the Great Expeditionary Office.

sentences.zh: 從達奚武征梁漢。

translations.literal: He followed Daxi Wu in campaigning against Liang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daxi Wu in the campaign against Liang and Han.

sentences.zh: 軍出，武令悅說其城主楊賢，悅乃貽之書，賢於是遂降。

translations.literal: When the army set out, Wu ordered Yue to persuade the city lord Yang Xian; Yue then sent him a letter, and Xian thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Wu had Wang Yue win over the city lord Yang Xian; Yue sent him a letter, and Xian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 悅又白武云：「白馬沖要，是必爭之地。

translations.literal: Yue also reported to Wu, saying: "Baima is a strategic choke point and a place rivals must fight over.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue also told Wu, "Baima is a vital choke point that enemies are sure to contest.

sentences.zh: 今城守寡弱，易可圖也。

translations.literal: Now the garrison is few and weak and easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Its garrison is thin and weak—it can be taken easily.

sentences.zh: 若蜀兵更至，攻之實難。」

translations.literal: If Liang troops come again, it will in truth be hard to attack.
translations.idiomatic: If Liang forces arrive first, the assault will be far harder.

sentences.zh: 武然之，即令悅率輕騎徑趣白馬。

translations.literal: Wu approved this and at once ordered Yue to lead light horse straight for Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Wu agreed and ordered Wang Yue to ride at once for Baima with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 悅示其禍福，梁將深悟，遂以城降。

translations.literal: Yue showed fortune and calamity; the Liang general deeply understood and thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue laid out the stakes; the Liang commander saw the point and surrendered the town.

sentences.zh: 時梁武陵王蕭紀果遣其將任珍奇，欲先據白馬。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, indeed sent his general Ren Zhenqi, wishing first to seize Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji had in fact sent Ren Zhenqi to seize Baima first.

sentences.zh: 行次關城，聞其已降，乃還。

translations.literal: Marching to Guan city, hearing it had already surrendered, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ren reached Guan city, learned Baima had already fallen, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 及梁州平，周文即以悅行刺史事。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, Emperor Wen of Zhou then made Yue act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified, Emperor Wen of Zhou put Wang Yue in charge as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 招攜初附，人吏安之。

translations.literal: He won over those who had just submitted; officials and people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He won over the newly submitted population until officials and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，徵還本任。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed emperor he was summoned back to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In year two of the deposed emperor's reign he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 屬改行台為中外府，尚書員廢，悅以儀同領兵還鄉里。

translations.literal: It happened that the expeditionary office was changed to the Central and Outer Office and the directorate of the ministry was abolished; Yue with Yitong rank led troops back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the expeditionary office became the Central and Outer Office and the ministry post was abolished, Wang Yue returned home leading troops as an officer of Yitong rank.

sentences.zh: 悅既久居顯職，及此之還，私懷怏怏，猶陵駕鄉里，失于宗黨之情，其長子康恃悅舊望，遂自驕縱。

translations.literal: Yue had long held eminent office; at this return he harbored private resentment, still lording it over his home district, failing in the feelings of his clan kin; his eldest son Kang relied on Yue's old standing and thereupon became proud and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Long accustomed to high office, he came home resentful, still bullying his neighbors and neglecting his kin; his eldest son Kang, trading on his father's prestige, grew arrogant and unbridled.

sentences.zh: 所部軍人將有婚禮，康乃非理陵辱。

translations.literal: A soldier of his command was about to hold a wedding; Kang then bullied and insulted him without reason.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier under his command was to marry, Kang bullied and humiliated him without cause.

sentences.zh: 軍人訴之，悅及康並坐除名，仍配遠防。

translations.literal: The soldier appealed; Yue and Kang both sat punished with removal from name and were still assigned to distant frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier appealed; father and son were both struck from the rolls and sent to distant frontier duty.

sentences.zh: 及於謹伐江陵，令悅從軍展效。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin campaigned against Jiangling, he ordered Yue to follow the army and display merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling, Wang Yue was ordered to follow the army and earn his way back.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，因留鎮之。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he was left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell he was left to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，依例復官，授郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, by precedent he was restored to office and appointed governor of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended, he was restored by precedent and made governor of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋拜使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、司水中大夫，進爵藍田縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Agile as Tiger, Director of the Office with the Third Rank of Honor, Grand Commander, and Si River Central Grand Master, and advanced to Marquis of Lantian county.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Agile as Tiger, Director of the Office with the Third Rank of Honor, Grand Commander, and Si River Central Grand Master, and raised to Marquis of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 俄遷司憲中大夫，賜姓宇文氏，又進爵河北縣公。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to Central Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice, granted the surname Yuwen, and again advanced to Duke of Hebei county.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly transferred to Central Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice, granted the surname Yuwen, and advanced again to Duke of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，不營生業，雖出內榮顯，家徒四壁而已，明帝手敕勞勉之。

translations.literal: His nature was frugal and restrained; he did not pursue livelihood; though he went out within and was glorious and eminent, his house had only four bare walls; Emperor Ming personally wrote an edict to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he never chased profit; though he rose to inner-court glory, his house held only bare walls—so Emperor Ming wrote him a personal edict of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year one he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子康嗣，官至司邑下大夫。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded; he reached the office of Si Yi Lower Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang inherited the line and rose to Si Yi Lower Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 趙文表，其先天水西人也，後徙居南鄭。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenbiao, his ancestors were men of Tianshui West, and later they moved to reside at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao—his forebears came from western Tianshui and later settled at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 累世為二千石。

translations.literal: For generations they were two-thousand-bushel officials.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held two-thousand-bushel offices.

sentences.zh: 父玨，性方嚴，有度量。

translations.literal: His father Jue was square and stern in nature, with measure and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jue was upright, stern, and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 位禦伯中大夫，封昌國縣伯。

translations.literal: His office reached Jibo Central Grand Master and he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changguo county.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jibo Central Grand Master and was created Baron of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 贈虞、絳二州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made governor of Yu and Jiang prefectures; his posthumous title is Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Yu and Jiang; his epithet was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 文表少而修謹，志存忠節。

translations.literal: Wenbiao in youth was cultivated and careful, his will set on loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao in youth was careful and cultivated, his heart set on loyalty.

sentences.zh: 起家為周文親信，累遷左金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He began his career as a trusted intimate of Emperor Wen of Zhou and was repeatedly promoted to Left Jinzi Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a trusted intimate of Emperor Wen of Zhou and rose to Left Jinzi Glory Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 保定五年，授畿伯下大夫，遷許國公宇文貴府長史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Baoding he was appointed Jibo Lower Grand Master and moved to be chief clerk in the mansion of Duke of Xu, Yuwen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year five he became Jibo Lower Grand Master and then chief clerk to Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui.

sentences.zh: 尋拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Cavalry General and Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Cavalry General with Yitong third rank.

sentences.zh: 仍從貴使突厥迎皇后，進止儀注，皆令文表典之。

translations.literal: He still followed Gui in going to the Türks to welcome the empress; the rules of advance and halt were all ordered to be managed by Wenbiao.
translations.idiomatic: He still followed Gui to the Türks to escort the empress home; every rule of march and halt was placed in Wenbiao's hands.

sentences.zh: 文表斟酌而行，皆合禮度。

translations.literal: Wenbiao weighed and carried them out; all accorded with ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao weighed each detail and carried them out, all in accord with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 及皇后將入境，突厥托以馬瘦徐行，文表慮其為變，遂說突厥使羅莫緣曰：「後自發彼蕃，已淹時序，途經沙漠，人馬疲勞，且東寇每伺間隙，吐谷渾亦能為變。

translations.literal: When the empress was about to enter the border, the Türks pleaded that the horses were lean and went slowly; Wenbiao feared they would make trouble and thereupon persuaded the Türk envoy Luomo Yuan, saying: "Since the empress set out from your realm, time has already dragged on; the road crossed the desert and men and horses are weary; moreover eastern enemies constantly watch for openings, and the Tuyuhun too can make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress neared the border the Türks claimed their horses were thin and slowed the march; fearing treachery, Wenbiao urged the Türk envoy Luomo Yuan: "Since Her Majesty left your realm time has already slipped; you have crossed the desert and men and horses are spent; eastern enemies watch for any opening, and the Tuyuhun too can strike.

sentences.zh: 今君以可汗愛女，結姻上國，曾無防慮，豈人臣之體乎？」

translations.literal: Now you, with the qaghan's beloved daughter, have formed a marriage alliance with the upper state, yet have no precaution at all—is this the deportment of a minister?
translations.idiomatic: You bring the qaghan's daughter into marriage with the Son of Heaven yet take no precautions—is that how a minister behaves?

sentences.zh: 莫緣然之，遂倍道兼行，數日至甘州。

translations.literal: Mo Yuan approved this and thereupon traveled day and night by double stages; in several days they reached Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luomo Yuan agreed; they doubled the pace and reached Ganzhou within days.

sentences.zh: 以迎後功，別封伯陽縣伯。

translations.literal: For the merit of welcoming the empress he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Boyang county.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the empress he was separately created Baron of Boyang.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，除梁州總管府長史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he was made chief clerk of the Liangzhou area commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year three he became chief clerk of the Liangzhou area headquarters.

sentences.zh: 所管地名恆稜者，方數百里，並夷、獠所居，恃其險固，常懷不軌，文表率眾討平之。

translations.literal: Among the districts he administered was one called Hengling, several hundred li square, all inhabited by Yi and Liao who relied on rugged terrain and constantly harbored disloyalty; Wenbiao led the masses to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: His district included Hengling, hundreds of li across, held by Yi and Liao who trusted the terrain and often rebelled; he led troops and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 遷蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: He was moved to be governor of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 政尚仁恕，夷、獠懷之。

translations.literal: His government esteemed benevolence and forgiveness; the Yi and Liao embraced him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with benevolence and forbearance, and the Yi and Liao came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was added Grand General Agile as Tiger and Director of the Office with the Third Rank of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Grand General Agile as Tiger with the third rank of court honor.

sentences.zh: 又加大將軍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand General and advanced in noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand General and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 大象中，拜吳州總管，時開府于顗為吳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era he was appointed area commander of Wu Prefecture; at that time the Director of the Office Yu Yan was governor of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he was made area commander of Wu while Yu Yan of the Director's Office was governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝執政，尉遲迥等舉兵，遠近騷然，人懷異望。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, Yu Chi Jiong and others raised troops; far and near were in turmoil and people harbored divergent hopes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui seized power, Yuchi Jiong and others rose in arms; the realm seethed and loyalties wavered.

sentences.zh: 顗自以族大，且為國家肺腑，懼文表負已，謀欲先之，乃稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Yan considered himself of great clan and also the state's close kin; he feared Wenbiao would turn against him and plotted to strike first; he then claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yan, counting himself great kin and close to the throne, feared Wenbiao would turn on him and plotted to strike first; he pleaded illness and stayed indoors.

sentences.zh: 文表往問之，顗遂手刃文表，因令其吏人告云：「文表謀反。」

translations.literal: Wenbiao went to inquire after him; Yan thereupon personally ran Wenbiao through with a blade and then ordered his clerks and people to report, saying: "Wenbiao plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Wenbiao came to visit, Yu Yan stabbed him with his own hand, then had his staff announce that Wenbiao had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仍馳啟其狀。

translations.literal: He still hurried to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent a rushed report to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以諸方未定，恐顗為變，遂授顗吳州總管以安之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the regions were not yet settled, feared Yan might change sides, and thereupon appointed Yan area commander of Wu Prefecture to settle him.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still unsettled, the emperor feared Yu Yan might turn rebel and appointed him area commander of Wu to keep him quiet.

sentences.zh: 後知文表無異志，雖不罪顗，而聽其子仁海襲爵。

translations.literal: Later knowing Wenbiao had no divergent will, though he did not punish Yan, he allowed his son Renhai to inherit the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Learning later that Wenbiao had been loyal, the court did not punish Yu Yan but let his son Renhai inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 元定，字願安，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding, style name Yuan'an, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding, courtesy name Yuan'an, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖比，魏婺州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bi was governor of Wu Prefecture in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bi had been governor of Wu in Wei.

sentences.zh: 父道龍，钜鹿郡守。

translations.literal: His father Daolong was governor of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daolong was governor of Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 定惇厚少言，內沈審而外剛毅。

translations.literal: Ding was sincere and thick, spoke little, inwardly deep and examining, outwardly firm and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding was steady and sparing of words, inwardly thoughtful and outwardly unyielding.

sentences.zh: 從周文討侯莫陳悅，以功拜步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wen of Zhou in campaigning against Hou Mo Chen Yue, by merit he was appointed Infantry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with Emperor Wen of Zhou against Hou Mo Chen Yue, he was made Infantry Commandant for his service.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，封高邑縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he was enfeoffed as Baronet of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Yuan Ding was created Baronet of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 定有勇略，累從征伐，每戰必陷陣，然未嘗自言其功。

translations.literal: Ding had courage and stratagem; he repeatedly followed campaigns, and in every battle he was sure to break the enemy line, yet he never himself spoke of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and resourceful, he fought in campaign after campaign and always broke the enemy line, yet never boasted of his deeds.

sentences.zh: 周文深重之，諸將亦稱其長者。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou deeply valued him; the generals also praised him as an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou held him in deep esteem; fellow commanders called him an elder worth respecting.

sentences.zh: 累加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly added Grand General Agile as Tiger and Director of the Office with the Third Rank of Honor and advanced in noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General Agile as Tiger with the third rank of honor and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，以宗室進封建城郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed emperor, by imperial clan standing he was advanced to Prince of Jiancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year two of the deposed emperor he was advanced, as imperial kin, to Prince of Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，行《周禮》，爵隨例降，改封長湖郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year the 《Rites of Zhou》 were implemented; noble ranks followed precedent and were lowered; he was changed to Duke of Changhu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, when the 《Rites of Zhou》 were enacted, titles were reduced by rule and he became Duke of Changhu.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，拜岷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was appointed governor of Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he was made governor of Min.

sentences.zh: 威恩兼濟，甚得羌豪之情，先時生羌據險不賓者，至是並出山谷，從征賦焉。

translations.literal: Authority and kindness were both applied; he greatly won the feelings of the Qiang chieftains; those raw Qiang who earlier held rugged terrain and would not submit now all came out of valleys and mountains to follow levies and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Blending awe with kindness, he won the Qiang chiefs; raw Qiang who had held the highlands now came down from the valleys to pay taxes and tribute.

sentences.zh: 及定代還，羌豪等咸戀慕之。

translations.literal: When Ding returned from acting as replacement, the Qiang chieftains all yearned for him with affection.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his acting post, the Qiang chiefs mourned his going.

sentences.zh: 保定中，授左宮伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was appointed Left Palace Baron Central Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoding era he became Left Palace Baron Central Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉左武伯中大夫，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Left Martial Baron Central Grand Master and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was made Left Martial Baron Central Grand Master and promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，陳湘州刺史華皎舉州歸梁，梁主欲因其隙更圖攻取，乃遣使請兵，詔定從衛公直率眾赴之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Hua Jiao, Liang governor of Xiangzhou, raised the province to submit to Liang; the Liang ruler wished to use the opening to scheme further attacks and thereupon sent envoys requesting troops; an edict ordered Ding to follow Duke of Wei Zhi in leading troops to go.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year two, Hua Jiao, Liang governor of Xiang, surrendered his province to Liang; the Liang ruler meant to exploit the moment and asked for Zhou troops; Yuan Ding was ordered to follow Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi.

sentences.zh: 梁人與華皎皆為水軍，定為陸軍，直總督之。

translations.literal: The men of Liang and Hua Jiao were all water forces; Ding was land force; Zhi overall commanded them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Hua Jiao fought as a river fleet; Yuan Ding commanded the land wing under Zhi's overall command.

sentences.zh: 俱至夏口，而陳郢州堅守不下，直令定圍之。

translations.literal: All reached Xiakou, but the Chen governor of E Prefecture held firm and would not fall; Zhi ordered Ding to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Xiakou, but Chen's Ezhou governor held out; Zhi ordered Yuan Ding to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 陳遣其將淳于量、徐度、吳明徹等水陸來拒，皎為陳人所敗，真得脫身歸梁。

translations.literal: Chen sent its generals Chunyu Liang, Xu Du, Wu Mingche, and others by land and water to resist; Jiao was defeated by the Chen men, and Zhen truly escaped body and returned to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Chunyu Liang, Xu Du, Wu Mingche, and others by land and water; Hua Jiao was beaten, though Zhen escaped back to Liang.

sentences.zh: 定既孤軍縣隔，進退無路，陳人乘勝，水陸逼之。

translations.literal: Ding was now an isolated army cut off; advance and retreat had no road; the Chen men seized victory and pressed by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding's force was isolated with no line of retreat; the Chen pressed their advantage by land and river.

sentences.zh: 定乃率所部，斫竹開路，且戰且行，欲趨湘州，而湘州已陷。

translations.literal: Ding thereupon led his command, hewing bamboo to open a road, fighting as he marched, wishing to hurry to Xiangzhou, but Xiangzhou had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men cutting bamboo to open a path, fighting as they marched toward Xiangzhou—but Xiangzhou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 徐度等知定窮迫，遣使偽與定通和，重為盟誓，許放還國。

translations.literal: Xu Du and the rest, knowing Ding was cornered, sent envoys falsely to treat with Ding, again making heavy oaths, promising to let him return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du, seeing him trapped, sent envoys with false offers of peace, solemn oaths, and promise of safe passage home.

sentences.zh: 定疑其詭詐，欲力戰死之。

translations.literal: Ding suspected their deceit and wished to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding suspected trickery and meant to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 而定長史長孫隆及諸將等多勸定和，定乃許之。

translations.literal: Yet Ding's chief clerk Zhangsun Long and the many generals mostly urged Ding to make peace; Ding thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: But his chief clerk Zhangsun Long and most of his officers urged peace, and he consented.

sentences.zh: 於是與度等刑牲歃血，解仗就船。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Du and the rest they slaughtered beasts and drank blood, laid down arms and boarded boats.
translations.idiomatic: He swore blood-oaths with Xu Du, laid down arms, and boarded their boats.

sentences.zh: 為度所執，所部眾軍亦被囚虜，送詣丹陽。

translations.literal: He was seized by Du; all the troops of his command were also imprisoned and captured and sent to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du seized him; his entire command was taken prisoner and sent to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 居數月，憂憤發病卒。

translations.literal: After several months he died of illness from grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he died of grief and rage in captivity.

sentences.zh: 子樂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Le succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Le inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 楊舣，字顯進，正平高涼人也。

translations.literal: Yang Biao, style name Xianjin, was a man of Gaoliang in Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao, courtesy name Xianjin, came from Gaoliang in Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 祖貴、父猛，並為縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui and father Meng were both county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui and father Meng had both been county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 舣少豪俠，有志氣。

translations.literal: Biao in youth was bold and chivalrous, with will and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yang Biao was bold and chivalrous, full of resolve.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，爾硃榮殺害朝士，大司馬、城陽王元徽逃難投舣，舣藏而免之。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, Erzhu Rong killed court gentlemen; the Grand Marshal, Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui, fled in distress and threw himself on Biao; Biao hid him and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Xiaochang, when Erzhu Rong slaughtered courtiers, Grand Marshal Yuan Hui, Prince of Chengyang, fled to Yang Biao for refuge; Biao hid him and he survived.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝立，徽乃出，復為司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was established, Hui then came forth and again became Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Hui emerged and resumed his post as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 由是舣以義烈，擢拜伏波將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: Because of this Biao, for righteous valor, was promoted and appointed Wave-Quelling General and Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For this loyal act Yang Biao was promoted to Wave-Quelling General and Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，孝莊北度太行。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaozhuang crossed the Taihang northward.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao seized Luoyang, Emperor Xiaozhuang fled north across the Taihang.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮奉帝南討，至馬渚，舣乃具船以濟王師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong escorted the emperor south to campaign, reaching Mazhu, Biao then prepared boats to ferry the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched the emperor south to campaign and reached Mazhu, Yang Biao gathered boats to ferry the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 顥平，封肥如縣伯，加鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉、行濟北郡事。

translations.literal: When Hao was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Feiru county and added Remote-Pacifying General, Infantry Commandant, and acting governor of Jibei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao was crushed he was created Baron of Feiru, made Remote-Pacifying General and Infantry Commandant, and given acting charge of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 進都督、平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Commander-in-Chief, Pacifying-East General, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Commander-in-Chief, Pacifying-East General, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 從孝武入關，進爵為侯，加撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xiaowu into Guan, he was advanced in noble rank to marquis and added Pacifying-Army General and Silver Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xiaowu into Guan, he was raised to marquis and made Pacifying-Army General with Silver Glory Grand Master rank.

sentences.zh: 時東魏遷鄴，周文欲知其所為，乃遣舣間行詣鄴以觀察之。

translations.literal: At that time Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye; Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to know what they were doing and thereupon sent Biao by secret route to Ye to observe.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Yang Biao in disguise to spy out their affairs.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，授通直散騎常侍、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Returning from the mission he matched the intent and was appointed Direct-Passing Regular Attendant and Grand Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His report pleased the throne; he was made Direct-Passing Regular Attendant and Grand Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 稽胡恃險不賓，屢行鈔竊，以舣兼黃門侍郎，往慰撫之。

translations.literal: The Ji Hu relied on rugged terrain and would not submit, repeatedly making raids; Biao was concurrently made Yellow Gate Attendant and sent to console and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Hu, trusting rough country, raided repeatedly; Yang Biao was also made Yellow Gate Attendant and sent to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 舣頗有權略，能得邊情，誘化酋梁，多來款附，乃有隨樹入朝者。

translations.literal: Biao was quite resourceful in power and stratagem, able to grasp border sentiment; he enticed and transformed chieftains, and many came to sincere submission; there were some who followed the trees into court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Resourceful and shrewd, he read the frontier well, won over tribal chiefs until many submitted—and some even entered court in their tree-bark dress.

sentences.zh: 時弘農為東魏守，舣從周文攻拔之。

translations.literal: At that time Hongnong was held by Eastern Wei; Biao followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in attacking and taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong was then held by Eastern Wei; Yang Biao followed Emperor Wen of Zhou and helped take it.

sentences.zh: 然自河以北，猶附東魏。

translations.literal: Yet from the river northward they still adhered to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: North of the river, however, many districts still obeyed Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 舣父猛先為邵郡白水令，舣與其豪右相知，請微行詣邵郡，舉兵以應朝廷。

translations.literal: Biao's father Meng had earlier been magistrate of Baishui in Shao commandery; Biao was acquainted with its powerful local families and requested to go in micro dress to Shao commandery and raise troops to respond to the court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng had once been magistrate of Baishui in Shao; Yang Biao knew the local strongmen there and asked to go in plain dress to Shao and raise troops for the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周文許之，舣遂行。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou permitted it; Biao thereupon set out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou agreed, and Yang Biao set out.

sentences.zh: 與土豪王覆憐等陰謀舉事，密相應會，內外俱發，遂拔邵郡，禽郡守程保及縣令四人，並斬之。

translations.literal: With the powerful local Wang Fulin and others he secretly plotted to raise the affair; they secretly responded to one another inside and outside, both sides rising together, and thereupon took Shao commandery, captured the governor Cheng Bao and four county magistrates, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: With the local magnate Wang Fulin and others he plotted in secret; when inner and outer parties rose together they seized Shao, took governor Cheng Bao and four county magistrates, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 眾議推舣行郡事，舣以因覆憐成事，遂表覆憐為邵郡守。

translations.literal: The masses deliberated and pushed Biao to act as governor; Biao because Fulin had accomplished the affair thereupon memorialized Fulin as governor of Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wanted Yang Biao to govern Shao, but since Wang Fulin had made the rising possible he memorialized Fulin as governor instead.

sentences.zh: 以功授大行台左丞，仍率義徒更為經略。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Great Expeditionary Office and still led the righteous bands in further strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Left Vice Director of the Great Expeditionary Office while still leading loyal levies in further operations.

sentences.zh: 於是遣諜人誘說東魏城堡，旬月之間，正平、河北、南汾、二絳、建州、太甯等諸城，並有請為內應者，大軍因攻而拔之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent spies to entice and persuade Eastern Wei walled cities; within a month or so the cities of Zhengping, Hebei, Southern Fen, the two Jiang, Jianzhou, and Taining, among others, all had some who requested to serve as inner responders, and the great army thereupon attacked and took them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to win over Eastern Wei garrisons; within a month Zhengping, Hebei, Southern Fen, the two Jiang districts, Jianzhou, Taining, and others had men offering to open their gates, and the main army stormed them in succession.

sentences.zh: 以舣行正平郡事，左丞如故。

translations.literal: Biao was made to act as governor of Zhengping commandery, the left vice directorate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao was made acting governor of Zhengping while keeping his vice-directorship.

sentences.zh: 齊神武敗于沙苑，其將韓軌、潘樂、可硃渾元等為殿，舣分兵要截，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu was defeated at Shayuan; his generals Han Gui, Pan Yue, and Kezhu Hun Yuan served as rear guard; Biao divided troops to intercept and kill and wound very many.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shenwu was beaten at Shayuan, his rearguard under Han Gui, Pan Yue, and Kezhu Hun Yuan was intercepted by Yang Biao's detachments, who killed and wounded great numbers.

sentences.zh: 東雍州刺史司馬恭懼舣威聲，棄城遁走。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei governor of Eastern Yongzhou, Sima Gong, feared Biao's martial renown and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yongzhou governor Sima Gong, fearing Yang Biao's reputation, abandoned his city and fled.

sentences.zh: 舣遂移據東雍州。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon shifted his base to Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao then moved his base to Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 周文以舣有謀略，堪委邊任，乃表行建州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because Biao had stratagem and could be entrusted with border duty, thereupon memorialized him to act as Jianzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Judging him fit for the frontier, Emperor Wen of Zhou had him memorialized to handle Jianzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 時建州遠在敵境，然舣威恩夙著，所經之處，多贏糧附之。

translations.literal: At that time Jianzhou was far in enemy territory, yet Biao's authority and kindness had long been manifest; wherever he passed, many carried extra grain to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou lay deep in enemy country, yet his fame for justice had long spread—wherever he marched, people brought extra grain to join him.

sentences.zh: 比至建州，眾已一萬。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Jianzhou, his followers already numbered ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Jianzhou he had ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 東魏州刺史車折于洛出兵逆戰，舣擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei governor Chezhe Yu Luo led troops out to meet him in battle; Biao defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei governor Chezhe Yu Luo marched out to fight; Yang Biao defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又破其行台斛律俱於州西，大獲甲仗及軍資，以給義士。

translations.literal: He again broke their expeditionary office commander Hulu Ju west of the prefecture and greatly obtained armor and military stores, giving them to the righteous bands.
translations.idiomatic: He also routed their expeditionary commander Hulu Ju west of the prefectural seat, seizing armor and supplies for his loyal levies.

sentences.zh: 由是威名大振。

translations.literal: Thereby his martial renown greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: His martial fame shook the region.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣太保尉景攻陷正平，復遣行台薛修義與斛律俱相會，於是敵眾漸盛。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Grand Guardian Wei Jing to attack and take Zhengping and again sent expeditionary office Xue Xiuyi to join with Hulu Ju; thereby the enemy masses gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Grand Guardian Wei Jing to retake Zhengping and expeditionary commander Xue Xiuyi to join Hulu Ju, and enemy strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 舣以孤軍無援，且腹背受敵，謀欲拔還，復恐義徒背叛，遂偽為周文書，遣人若從外送來者，雲已遣軍四道赴援。

translations.literal: Biao with an isolated army without relief, and moreover receiving enemies front and back, plotted to pull back, yet again feared the righteous bands would turn traitor; he thereupon forged a letter of Emperor Wen of Zhou and sent a man as if it had been delivered from outside, saying he had already sent armies on four roads to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated, attacked front and rear, he planned to withdraw yet feared his levies would desert; he forged a letter from Emperor Wen of Zhou and had a courier arrive as if from outside, claiming four relief columns were already marching.

sentences.zh: 因令人漏泄，使所在知之。

translations.literal: He then had men leak it so that wherever they were, they would know.
translations.idiomatic: He leaked the news so every district heard it.

sentences.zh: 又分士人義酋，令各領所部四出鈔掠，擬供軍費。

translations.literal: He again divided gentry and righteous chieftains, ordering each to lead his own following in four directions to raid and plunder, intending to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent local gentry and loyal chiefs out in four directions to raid for supplies.

sentences.zh: 舣分遣訖，遂於夜中拔還邵郡。

translations.literal: When Biao had finished dividing and sending them, he thereupon in the middle of the night pulled back to Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once his detachments were away, he slipped back to Shao in the dead of night.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其權以全軍。

translations.literal: The court praised his resourcefulness in preserving the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his cunning in saving his whole force.

sentences.zh: 既授建州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed governor of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made governor of Jian.

sentences.zh: 時東魏以正平為東雍州，遣薛榮祖鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time Eastern Wei made Zhengping into Eastern Yongzhou and sent Xue Rongzu to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had turned Zhengping into Eastern Yongzhou and put Xue Rongzu in command.

sentences.zh: 乃先遣奇兵，急攻汾橋。

translations.literal: He first sent picked troops to hurry and attack Fen Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao first sent picked troops in a rush against Fen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 榮祖果盡出城中戰士，于汾橋拒守。

translations.literal: Rongzu indeed led out all the city's warriors; at Fen Bridge he held defense.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu duly marched out every fighting man to hold Fen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其夜，舣從他道濟，遂襲克之。

translations.literal: That night Biao crossed by another route and thereupon made a surprise attack and took it.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yang Biao crossed by another route and stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 邵郡人以郡東叛，郡守郭武安脫身走免。

translations.literal: The men of Shao commandery because the east of the commandery rebelled, the commandery governor Guo Wu'an slipped body and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Shao rebelled, commandery governor Guo Wu'an fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 舣又率兵攻而復之。

translations.literal: Biao again led troops to attack and recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao led troops back and recovered the district.

sentences.zh: 轉正平郡守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 又擊破東魏南絳郡，虜其郡守屈僧珍。

translations.literal: He again broke Eastern Wei's Southern Jiang commandery and captured its governor Qu Sengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He also smashed Eastern Wei's Southern Jiang and took its governor Qu Sengzhen.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，封郃陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Recording his former and later merit, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Heyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Tallying his past and recent service, he was created Baron of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，舣攻拔標栢穀塢，因即鎮之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mangshan he attacked and took the Biaobai Valley stockade and thereupon garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: At Mangshan he stormed the Biaobai Valley stockade and held it.

sentences.zh: 及大軍不利，舣亦拔還。

translations.literal: When the great army met adversity, Biao also pulled back.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army met disaster, Yang Biao withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 而東魏將侯景率騎追舣，舣與儀同韋法保同心抗禦，且戰且前，景乃引退。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Hou Jing led horse in pursuit of Biao; Biao with the Yitong Wei Fabao with one heart resisted, fighting as they advanced, and Jing then led away his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing of Eastern Wei pursued with cavalry; Yang Biao and Wei Fabao, a fellow officer of Yitong rank, fought shoulder to shoulder until Jing drew off.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，復授建州刺史，鎮軍箱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised this and again appointed him governor of Jian Prefecture, garrisoning the military chest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou commended him and again made him governor of Jian, guarding the strategic depot.

sentences.zh: 舣久從軍役，末及葬父。

translations.literal: Biao had long followed military service and had not yet buried his father.
translations.idiomatic: Long on campaign, he had never buried his father.

sentences.zh: 至是，表請遷葬。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized requesting to move the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He now asked leave to rebury his father.

sentences.zh: 詔贈其父車騎大將軍、儀同三司、晉州刺史，贈其母夏陽縣君，並給儀衛，州裏榮之。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made his father Grand Cavalry General, Yitong Third Rank, and governor of Jin Prefecture; his mother was posthumously made Lady of Xiayang county; both were given ceremonial guards; the district was honored by this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously made his father Grand Cavalry General with Yitong third rank and governor of Jin, his mother Lady of Xiayang, and granted ceremonial guards—the district took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武圍玉壁，別令侯景趣齊子嶺。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu besieged Yubi, he separately ordered Hou Jing to hurry toward Qizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shenwu besieged Yubi he also sent Hou Jing toward Qizi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 舣恐入寇邵郡，率騎禦之。

translations.literal: Biao feared he would enter and raid Shao commandery and led horse to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a raid on Shao, Yang Biao rode out to block him.

sentences.zh: 景遠聞舣至，斫木斷路者六十餘里，猶驚而不安，遂退還河陽，其見憚如此。

translations.literal: Jing from afar heard Biao had come, felled trees and blocked the road for more than sixty li, yet was still alarmed and uneasy, and thereupon retreated to Heyang; such was the degree to which he was feared.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, hearing Yang Biao was coming, felled trees across sixty li of road yet still could not steady his nerves and retreated to Heyang—such was the fear he inspired.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進授大都督，加晉、建二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was advanced to Grand Commander and added military affairs of Jin and Jian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he was made Grand Commander with military authority over Jin and Jian.

sentences.zh: 又攻破蓼塢，獲東魏將李顯，進儀同三司。

translations.literal: He again broke the Liaowu stockade and captured the Eastern Wei general Li Xian; he was advanced to Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Liaowu stockade, captured Eastern Wei general Li Xian, and was raised to Yitong third rank.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府，復鎮邵郡。

translations.literal: Soon he was added Director of the Office and again garrisoned Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director of the Office and again garrisoned Shao.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東討，授大行台尚書，率義眾先驅敵境，攻其四戍，拔之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the great army campaigned east; he was appointed Director of the Great Expeditionary Office and led the righteous masses as vanguard into enemy territory, attacking their four outposts and taking them.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen, during the eastern campaign, he became Director of the Great Expeditionary Office and led loyal levies as vanguard into enemy country, storming four outposts.

sentences.zh: 時以齊軍不出，乃追舣還。

translations.literal: At that time because the Qi army did not come out, they then recalled Biao back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi army failed to appear, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 改封華陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He was changed to Marquis of Huayang county.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Marquis of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 又于邵郡置邵州，以舣為刺史，率所部兵鎮之。

translations.literal: Also at Shao commandery they established Shao Prefecture, with Biao as governor, leading the troops of his command to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Prefecture was created with Yang Biao as governor, commanding his own troops in garrison.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，遷少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was moved to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year four he was made Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍圍洛陽，詔舣出軹關。

translations.literal: That year the great army besieged Luoyang; an edict ordered Biao out through Zhiguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the main force besieged Luoyang, he was ordered out through Zhiguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 然舣自鎮東境二十餘年，數與齊人戰，每常克獲，以此遂有輕敵之心。

translations.literal: Yet Biao himself had garrisoned the eastern marches for more than twenty years, repeatedly fighting the men of Qi, and every time usually achieved victory and booty; thereby he came to have a heart that belittled the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He had guarded the eastern frontier for twenty years, fighting Qi again and again and usually winning—so he grew contemptuous of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽未下，而舣深入敵境，又不設備。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang was not yet taken, yet Biao penetrated deep into enemy territory and again made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had not yet fallen, yet he plunged deep into enemy country without precautions.

sentences.zh: 齊人奄至，大破舣軍。

translations.literal: The men of Qi came suddenly; they greatly defeated Biao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forces struck suddenly and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 舣以眾敗，遂降于舣齊。

translations.literal: With his masses defeated, he then surrendered to Yi Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he surrendered to Qi.

sentences.zh: 舣之立勳也。

translations.literal: As for Biao's establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Biao had been building his reputation.

sentences.zh: 有慷慨壯烈之志，及軍敗，遂就虜以求苟免，時論以此鄙之，朝廷猶錄其功，不以為罪，令其子襲爵。

translations.literal: He had a generous and heroic will; when the army was defeated he then turned to the captors to seek a meager escape; contemporary opinion for this despised him, yet the court still recorded his merit and did not treat it as crime, ordering his son to inherit the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He had shown a generous, heroic spirit; after defeat he threw himself on the enemy to scrape by—a choice contemporaries despised, though the court still honored his past service, did not treat him as a traitor, and let his son inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 論曰：申徽局量深沉，文之以經史，陸通鑒悟明敏，飾之以溫恭，並夙奉龍顏，早蒙任遇，效宣提戟，功預披荊，義結周旋，恩生契闊。

translations.literal: The discourse says: Shen Hui's measure and capacity were deep and calm; he adorned it with the classics and histories. Lu Tong's insight and awareness were bright and keen; he decorated it with warmth and respect. Both early served the dragon countenance and early received appointment and favor; they exerted effort raising the halberd, their achievement anticipating the clearing of brambles; righteousness bound them in constant companionship, favor born in trials of separation.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Shen Hui was deep and measured, his mind furnished with the classics; Lu Tong was perceptive and quick, his manner graced with warmth. Both had served the throne from early days, borne arms in the founding struggles, and kept faith through hardship and parting.

sentences.zh: 遂得入居端揆，出撫列籓。

translations.literal: They were thereby able to enter and occupy the chief ministers' seats and go out to soothe the various fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they rose to the highest ministries and went out to govern the provinces.

sentences.zh: 雖以識用成名，抑亦情兼惟舊。

translations.literal: Though they became famous by insight and employment, they were also favored for old affection.
translations.idiomatic: They won fame by talent, yet also by long-standing favor.

sentences.zh: 陸逞於戎旅之際，以文雅見知，出境播延譽之能，蒞官著從政之美，曆居顯要，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Lu Cheng amid military affairs was known for literary elegance; going abroad he spread the ability of extending reputation; taking office he showed the beauty of following government; passing through eminent and important posts—was it for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng, even in camp, was known for culture; abroad he spread his good name, in office he showed sound governance—his long tenure in high posts was no accident!

sentences.zh: 厙狄峙建和戎之功，楊薦成入關之策，趙剛之克剪凶狡，趙昶之懷服氐、羌，王悅之料侯景，文表之譎突厥，或明稱先覺，或識表見機，觀其立功立事，皆一時志力之士也。

translations.literal: She Dishi established the achievement of harmonizing with the barbarians; Yang Jian accomplished the plan of entering Guan; Zhao Gang's ability to cut down the fierce and cunning; Zhao Chang's embracing and subduing the Di and Qiang; Wang Yue's foreseeing Hou Jing; Wenbiao's outwitting the Türks—or clearly called foreknowing, or showing insight and seizing the moment—view their establishing achievement and affairs: all were men of will and strength for their time.
translations.idiomatic: She Dishi won peace with the barbarians; Yang Jian devised the entry into Guan; Zhao Gang cut down the vicious; Zhao Chang won the Di and Qiang; Wang Yue foresaw Hou Jing's treachery; Zhao Wenbiao outwitted the Türks—some famed for foresight, some for reading the moment—all were men of decisive will in their age.

sentences.zh: 元定敗亡，同黃權之無路；

translations.literal: Yuan Ding defeated and perished, together with Huang Quan having no road;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding was ruined and trapped, like Huang Quan with no way out;

sentences.zh: 楊舣攻勝，亦兵破而身囚。

translations.literal: Yang Biao attacked and won, yet also with army broken and body imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao had won battles, yet in the end his army was broken and he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 功名寥落，良可嗟矣！

translations.literal: Merit and fame sparse and fallen—truly worth sighing over!
translations.idiomatic: Merit and fame thus scattered—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「師出以律，否臧凶。」

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says: "The army sets out by discipline; if not so, misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Changes》 says, "An army must march by discipline; without it, misfortune follows.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「不備不虞，不可以師。」

translations.literal: The 《Commentary》 says: "Without preparation and without precaution, one cannot lead an army."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Commentary》 says, "Without readiness and without forethought, one must not take the field."

sentences.zh: 其舣之謂也！

translations.literal: This is what is meant by Biao!
translations.idiomatic: That was Yang Biao's case exactly!
